{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json",
    "title": "Failover and Security Boundaries (Data Residency, Audit Logging, and Cross-Region Routing)",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Failover and Security Boundaries (Data Residency, Audit Logging, and Cross-Region Routing)\",\n  \"space\": \"security-and-compliance\",\n  \"author\": \"Miles Thornton\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"security\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"confidentiality\": \"restricted\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-07\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-02-12\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Sean Gallagher\",\n    \"Rafael Mendes\",\n    \"Mina Haddad\",\n    \"Victor Alvarez\",\n    \"Simran Kaur\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"security\",\n    \"reliability\",\n    \"failover\",\n    \"data-residency\",\n    \"routing\",\n    \"audit-logging\",\n    \"enterprise\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/region-health-service.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/multi-region-availability-slo-2026.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/regional-failover-communication-playbook.json\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"## Purpose\\nThis document defines **security boundaries that must be preserved during regional failover** for Redwood Inference (Hosted API and Dedicated). It specifies:\\n- How **data residency constraints** restrict routing/failover.\\n- **Audit logging** requirements for automated and manual failover actions.\\n- Guardrails for **cross-region routing** by customer tier (especially Enterprise and regulated workloads).\\n\\nThis guidance is mandatory for:\\n- Smart routing and policy engine changes that can influence region selection.\\n- Failover automation controller behavior (including dry-run and simulation modes).\\n- On-call execution and controlled failover tests (\\\"game days\\\").\\n\\n## Scope / Non-scope\\n**In scope**\\n- Hosted API and Dedicated failover behavior across Redwood-managed regions.\\n- Data residency enforcement at routing and control-plane policy layers.\\n- Audit events, retention, and access control for failover decisioning.\\n\\n**Out of scope**\\n- Customer-specific Private deployment automation (see Private guidance). This doc provides patterns only.\\n- Changes to customer contracts/SLA language (handled separately).\\n\\n## Definitions\\n- **Region**: A cloud provider region (e.g., us-east, eu-west).\\n- **Residency boundary**: The allowed set of regions in which a tenant\\u2019s **inference data plane** traffic may be processed.\\n- **Data plane**: Prompts, model inputs, outputs, embeddings, and tool/function payloads processed by inference.\\n- **Control plane**: Tenant metadata, config, quotas, routing policy config, and operational telemetry.\\n- **Failover**: Automatic or operator-approved routing change that shifts traffic from a primary region to another region.\\n- **Enterprise tier**: Contracted customers with security requirements (auditability, residency, notification expectations).\\n\\n## Security principles (must-haves)\\n1) **Residency first**: If a tenant has a residency constraint, failover MUST stay within that boundary. Availability must be achieved *within* the allowed set; otherwise we prefer **graceful degradation** (e.g., 503 + Retry-After) over violating residency.\\n2) **Explicit allow-listing**: Cross-region routing must be controlled by explicit configuration per tenant (or per org) and audited.\\n3) **Least privilege and separation of duties**: Only designated on-call/SRE roles may initiate or approve production failover actions. Changes to residency boundaries require Security approval.\\n4) **Audit everything**: Every recommendation, execution, rollback, and override must emit a structured audit event with enough evidence to reconstruct \\u201cwho/what/why/when/impact.\\u201d\\n5) **Deterministic policy evaluation**: Given the same inputs, routing policy evaluation must produce the same output (to enable security review, auditability, and predictable enforcement).\\n\\n## Data residency policy\\n### Residency categories\\nRedwood supports the following residency categories for the **inference data plane** (prompts/outputs/embeddings):\\n\\n| Category | Description | Example allowed regions | Example prohibited regions |\\n|---|---|---|---|\\n| Global (no residency) | Tenant allows processing in any supported region | us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast | none |\\n| US-only | Processing restricted to US regions | us-east, us-west | eu-west |\\n| EU-only | Processing restricted to EU regions | eu-west, eu-central | us-east |\\n| Region-pinned | Processing restricted to a single region | eu-west only | all others |\\n| Custom boundary | Contract-defined set | (explicit per tenant) | all non-listed |\\n\\nNotes:\\n- Residency applies to **data plane processing**. Control-plane metadata may be replicated as needed for availability, but must follow the data classification and storage policies in Security standards.\\n- Region naming above is conceptual; the authoritative list is in routing config.\\n\\n### Default behavior by tier\\n- **Self-serve / Standard Hosted**: Default category is **Global**, unless the tenant explicitly configures otherwise.\\n- **Enterprise Hosted**: Default category is **Global**, but residency constraints may be contractually required (EU-only, US-only, or Custom boundary). These constraints MUST be encoded as enforceable routing policies.\\n- **Dedicated**: Default category follows the contracted deployment footprint. Failover is restricted to the customer\\u2019s approved Dedicated regions.\\n- **Private**: Residency enforcement is the customer\\u2019s responsibility, but Redwood-provided guidance should mirror the principles in this document.\\n\\n## Cross-region failover rules\\n### Hard rules (never violate)\\n1) **Do not route data plane traffic outside the tenant\\u2019s residency boundary.**\\n2) **Do not \\u201ctemporarily\\u201d violate residency to restore availability.** If no in-boundary failover target is healthy, degrade service within the boundary.\\n3) **Do not change residency boundaries during an incident** to work around a capacity/regional outage unless:\\n   - Approved by Security (delegate on-call) AND\\n   - Approved by the customer (if Enterprise/regulated) AND\\n   - Documented in an incident timeline with explicit timestamps and scope.\\n\\n### Allowed failover patterns\\n- **Within-boundary failover** (preferred):\\n  - EU-only: eu-west \\u2192 eu-central\\n  - US-only: us-east \\u2192 us-west\\n  - Custom: primary \\u2192 secondary (both explicitly allow-listed)\\n- **Region-pinned tenants**:\\n  - No cross-region failover. Use load shedding and communicate impairment.\\n\\n### Decision hierarchy interaction (security perspective)\\nRouting may decide to fail over due to reachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, or capacity exhaustion; however:\\n- The policy engine MUST apply **residency gating as an absolute precondition** before evaluating \\u201cbest\\u201d region.\\n- If the \\u201cbest available\\u201d region is outside boundary, the decision must become **DEGRADE** (or keep traffic in-region with protective measures), not \\u201cfail over.\\u201d\\n\\n## Implementation requirements (routing, controller, and configs)\\n### Residency gating in the policy engine\\nThe policy engine must support a first-class predicate (conceptual):\\n- `allowed_regions(tenant_id)` returns a stable allow-list.\\n- Region selection must be `candidate_regions = healthy_regions \\u2229 allowed_regions`.\\n- If `candidate_regions` is empty, policy result must be one of:\\n  - `DEGRADE_WITHIN_BOUNDARY` (e.g., return 503/429 with Retry-After, reduce max tokens, disable optional features), or\\n  - `STAY_PUT_WITH_PROTECTION` (tight circuit breakers and load shedding), depending on product behavior.\\n\\nSecurity requirement: the code path must be **provably non-bypassable** (no \\u201cemergency override\\u201d without producing an audit event and requiring explicit approvals).\\n\\n### Configuration source of truth\\nFor Hosted and Dedicated:\\n- Residency boundary configuration must be stored in a **controlled configuration system** with:\\n  - Change review (required reviewers include Security for any boundary-tightening/loosening).\\n  - Immutable change history.\\n  - Rollback support.\\n\\n### Dedicated-specific constraints\\nDedicated customers may have:\\n- Hard region allow-lists bound to capacity pools.\\n- Explicit \\u201cno failover without approval\\u201d requirements.\\n\\nFailover automation for Dedicated must:\\n- Respect pool-level constraints (do not shift load to a pool not designated for that tenant).\\n- Coordinate with drain/evacuation procedures without exposing cross-tenant data.\\n\\n## Audit logging requirements\\n### What must be logged\\nAll systems participating in failover must emit structured events for:\\n- Recommendation (dry-run computation)\\n- Execution (policy flip applied)\\n- Rollback (automated or manual)\\n- Override (operator forcing a decision)\\n- Blocked action (attempted failover rejected due to residency boundary)\\n\\n### Required fields (minimum)\\nEach audit event must include (as applicable):\\n- **event_type**: recommend | execute | rollback | override | blocked\\n- **timestamp_utc**\\n- **tenant_id / org_id** (or an internal stable identifier)\\n- **tenant_tier**: self_serve | enterprise | dedicated\\n- **residency_category**: global | us_only | eu_only | region_pinned | custom\\n- **primary_region**, **target_region** (target may be empty for blocked/degrade)\\n- **decision**: failover | degrade | stay_put\\n- **reason_code**: reachability | error_burn | latency_burn | capacity | manual\\n- **evidence_refs**: links/IDs to region health snapshots, burn-rate alert IDs, probe runs\\n- **actor**: automation_controller | user:<id>\\n- **approval_state**: not_required | pending | approved | denied\\n- **change_id**: routing policy config revision / feature flag revision\\n- **correlation_ids**: incident_id (if any), request_id samples (optional), dashboard annotation ID\\n\\n### Retention and access\\n- Default retention (internal): **180 days** for audit events.\\n- Enterprise add-on / compliance packages: **\\u2265 400 days** retention, unless otherwise specified.\\n- Access must be restricted to:\\n  - SRE on-call and routing/control-plane engineers with an operational need\\n  - Security & compliance for audits and investigations\\n  - Customer Success only via approved exports/redactions (no raw prompt data)\\n\\n### Data minimization\\nAudit events must not include:\\n- Prompt text, model outputs, embeddings, or customer payloads.\\n- Customer secrets (API keys, tokens).\\n\\nIf request samples are needed for investigation, use approved secure logging mechanisms and follow incident response data handling procedures.\\n\\n## Handling of regulated / data-residency constrained customers\\n### If a region impairment occurs within a constrained boundary\\nExample: EU-only customer and eu-west is impaired.\\n- If eu-central is healthy and has capacity: **fail over to eu-central**.\\n- If no EU region is healthy/capable: **degrade within EU**.\\n  - Return 503 + Retry-After (preferred for overload)\\n  - Enforce stricter rate limits / max tokens for fairness\\n  - Disable non-essential optional features if supported by product policy\\n\\n### Communication expectations (Enterprise)\\n- During a real incident: follow the Regional Failover Communication Playbook.\\n- For planned tests: notify only customers whose traffic might be impacted, and explicitly state that residency boundaries will not be violated.\\n- If any customer perceives cross-region behavior, immediately:\\n  - Pull audit events for the tenant\\n  - Validate residency gating decisions\\n  - Engage Security and Support escalation\\n\\n## Controlled failover tests (\\u201cgame days\\u201d) security requirements\\nPrior to production tests:\\n1) Confirm residency gating is active and validated in staging.\\n2) Explicitly exclude region-pinned and regulated tenants unless written approval is obtained.\\n3) Ensure audit events and dashboard annotations are functioning.\\n4) Validate that \\u201cblocked due to residency\\u201d is observable (metric + audit event).\\n\\nDuring the test:\\n- Any attempted out-of-boundary action must be treated as a **SEV-2 security incident** if it results in data plane processing outside the boundary.\\n\\nAfter the test:\\n- Export the audit event summary for the test window and attach it to the game day results doc.\\n\\n## Operational checklist (on-call)\\nWhen failover automation suggests a policy change:\\n1) Identify tenant tier and residency category.\\n2) Confirm proposed target region is in allow-list.\\n3) Confirm automation approval requirements (some Enterprise/Dedicated tenants require ack).\\n4) Verify audit event emission is healthy (controller + policy engine).\\n5) Execute or approve.\\n6) If boundary prevents failover, choose degrade/stay-put path and update incident comms accordingly.\\n\\n## Examples\\n### Example A: Enterprise EU-only tenant during us-east incident\\n- Primary region: us-east (should not happen for EU-only; indicates misconfiguration)\\n- Required action:\\n  - Immediately block and correct routing policy (within incident change management)\\n  - File Security follow-up for residency misconfiguration\\n  - Confirm no data plane processing occurred outside EU via audit/telemetry\\n\\n### Example B: Global tenant during eu-west reachability failure\\n- Primary: eu-west\\n- Allowed: any region\\n- Action: fail over to us-east (or nearest healthy region by policy), emit audit events for recommend + execute + any rollback.\\n\\n### Example C: Region-pinned tenant when region is impaired\\n- Primary: eu-west\\n- Allowed: eu-west only\\n- Action: do not fail over. Enable protective controls (circuit breakers, load shedding), return Retry-After, and communicate impact.\\n\\n## Monitoring requirements (security-relevant)\\nMinimum dashboards/alerts needed:\\n- Count of `failover_blocked_due_to_residency` by tier\\n- Audit event delivery health (ingest lag, drop rate)\\n- Unauthorized/rare overrides (manual force actions)\\n- Drift detection: tenants with residency=EU-only receiving any non-EU routing decisions (should be zero)\\n\\n## Ownership and change control\\n- Owner: **Security & Compliance** (in partnership with SRE Reliability)\\n- Routing enforcement: **Smart Routing** team (Mina Haddad) + Policy engine owner (Jordan Lee)\\n- Audit event pipeline: **SRE / Observability** (Allison Grant)\\n\\nChanges to this document require review from:\\n- Security & Compliance\\n- SRE Reliability lead (Sean Gallagher or delegate)\\n- Routing policy tech lead (Ravi Menon)\\n\\n## Open questions / follow-ups\\n- Define a standard \\u201ccustom boundary\\u201d representation shared between Hosted and Dedicated policy configs.\\n- Confirm enterprise retention defaults for audit logs align with compliance add-ons.\\n- Add automated drift checks that continuously validate residency enforcement using synthetic tenant policies (no customer data).\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349\"\n}",

document.title: Failover and Security Boundaries (Data Residency, Audit Logging, and Cross-Region Routing)

{
  "title": "Failover and Security Boundaries (Data Residency, Audit Logging, and Cross-Region Routing)",
  "space": "security-and-compliance",
  "author": "Miles Thornton",
  "owner_team": "security",
  "status": "published",
  "confidentiality": "restricted",
  "created_at": "2026-01-07",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-12",
  "reviewers": [
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Rafael Mendes",
    "Mina Haddad",
    "Victor Alvarez",
    "Simran Kaur"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "security",
    "reliability",
    "failover",
    "data-residency",
    "routing",
    "audit-logging",
    "enterprise"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy.json",
    "sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-platform/systems-and-services/region-health-service.json",
    "sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/multi-region-availability-slo-2026.json",
    "sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/regional-failover-communication-playbook.json"
  ],
  "content": "## Purpose
This document defines **security boundaries that must be preserved during regional failover** for Redwood Inference (Hosted API and Dedicated). It specifies:
- How **data residency constraints** restrict routing/failover.
- **Audit logging** requirements for automated and manual failover actions.
- Guardrails for **cross-region routing** by customer tier (especially Enterprise and regulated workloads).

This guidance is mandatory for:
- Smart routing and policy engine changes that can influence region selection.
- Failover automation controller behavior (including dry-run and simulation modes).
- On-call execution and controlled failover tests ("game days").

## Scope / Non-scope
**In scope**
- Hosted API and Dedicated failover behavior across Redwood-managed regions.
- Data residency enforcement at routing and control-plane policy layers.
- Audit events, retention, and access control for failover decisioning.

**Out of scope**
- Customer-specific Private deployment automation (see Private guidance). This doc provides patterns only.
- Changes to customer contracts/SLA language (handled separately).

## Definitions
- **Region**: A cloud provider region (e.g., us-east, eu-west).
- **Residency boundary**: The allowed set of regions in which a tenant’s **inference data plane** traffic may be processed.
- **Data plane**: Prompts, model inputs, outputs, embeddings, and tool/function payloads processed by inference.
- **Control plane**: Tenant metadata, config, quotas, routing policy config, and operational telemetry.
- **Failover**: Automatic or operator-approved routing change that shifts traffic from a primary region to another region.
- **Enterprise tier**: Contracted customers with security requirements (auditability, residency, notification expectations).

## Security principles (must-haves)
1) **Residency first**: If a tenant has a residency constraint, failover MUST stay within that boundary. Availability must be achieved *within* the allowed set; otherwise we prefer **graceful degradation** (e.g., 503 + Retry-After) over violating residency.
2) **Explicit allow-listing**: Cross-region routing must be controlled by explicit configuration per tenant (or per org) and audited.
3) **Least privilege and separation of duties**: Only designated on-call/SRE roles may initiate or approve production failover actions. Changes to residency boundaries require Security approval.
4) **Audit everything**: Every recommendation, execution, rollback, and override must emit a structured audit event with enough evidence to reconstruct “who/what/why/when/impact.”
5) **Deterministic policy evaluation**: Given the same inputs, routing policy evaluation must produce the same output (to enable security review, auditability, and predictable enforcement).

## Data residency policy
### Residency categories
Redwood supports the following residency categories for the **inference data plane** (prompts/outputs/embeddings):

| Category | Description | Example allowed regions | Example prohibited regions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Global (no residency) | Tenant allows processing in any supported region | us-east, us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast | none |
| US-only | Processing restricted to US regions | us-east, us-west | eu-west |
| EU-only | Processing restricted to EU regions | eu-west, eu-central | us-east |
| Region-pinned | Processing restricted to a single region | eu-west only | all others |
| Custom boundary | Contract-defined set | (explicit per tenant) | all non-listed |

Notes:
- Residency applies to **data plane processing**. Control-plane metadata may be replicated as needed for availability, but must follow the data classification and storage policies in Security standards.
- Region naming above is conceptual; the authoritative list is in routing config.

### Default behavior by tier
- **Self-serve / Standard Hosted**: Default category is **Global**, unless the tenant explicitly configures otherwise.
- **Enterprise Hosted**: Default category is **Global**, but residency constraints may be contractually required (EU-only, US-only, or Custom boundary). These constraints MUST be encoded as enforceable routing policies.
- **Dedicated**: Default category follows the contracted deployment footprint. Failover is restricted to the customer’s approved Dedicated regions.
- **Private**: Residency enforcement is the customer’s responsibility, but Redwood-provided guidance should mirror the principles in this document.

## Cross-region failover rules
### Hard rules (never violate)
1) **Do not route data plane traffic outside the tenant’s residency boundary.**
2) **Do not “temporarily” violate residency to restore availability.** If no in-boundary failover target is healthy, degrade service within the boundary.
3) **Do not change residency boundaries during an incident** to work around a capacity/regional outage unless:
   - Approved by Security (delegate on-call) AND
   - Approved by the customer (if Enterprise/regulated) AND
   - Documented in an incident timeline with explicit timestamps and scope.

### Allowed failover patterns
- **Within-boundary failover** (preferred):
  - EU-only: eu-west → eu-central
  - US-only: us-east → us-west
  - Custom: primary → secondary (both explicitly allow-listed)
- **Region-pinned tenants**:
  - No cross-region failover. Use load shedding and communicate impairment.

### Decision hierarchy interaction (security perspective)
Routing may decide to fail over due to reachability, 5xx burn, tail latency burn, or capacity exhaustion; however:
- The policy engine MUST apply **residency gating as an absolute precondition** before evaluating “best” region.
- If the “best available” region is outside boundary, the decision must become **DEGRADE** (or keep traffic in-region with protective measures), not “fail over.”

## Implementation requirements (routing, controller, and configs)
### Residency gating in the policy engine
The policy engine must support a first-class predicate (conceptual):
- `allowed_regions(tenant_id)` returns a stable allow-list.
- Region selection must be `candidate_regions = healthy_regions ∩ allowed_regions`.
- If `candidate_regions` is empty, policy result must be one of:
  - `DEGRADE_WITHIN_BOUNDARY` (e.g., return 503/429 with Retry-After, reduce max tokens, disable optional features), or
  - `STAY_PUT_WITH_PROTECTION` (tight circuit breakers and load shedding), depending on product behavior.

Security requirement: the code path must be **provably non-bypassable** (no “emergency override” without producing an audit event and requiring explicit approvals).

### Configuration source of truth
For Hosted and Dedicated:
- Residency boundary configuration must be stored in a **controlled configuration system** with:
  - Change review (required reviewers include Security for any boundary-tightening/loosening).
  - Immutable change history.
  - Rollback support.

### Dedicated-specific constraints
Dedicated customers may have:
- Hard region allow-lists bound to capacity pools.
- Explicit “no failover without approval” requirements.

Failover automation for Dedicated must:
- Respect pool-level constraints (do not shift load to a pool not designated for that tenant).
- Coordinate with drain/evacuation procedures without exposing cross-tenant data.

## Audit logging requirements
### What must be logged
All systems participating in failover must emit structured events for:
- Recommendation (dry-run computation)
- Execution (policy flip applied)
- Rollback (automated or manual)
- Override (operator forcing a decision)
- Blocked action (attempted failover rejected due to residency boundary)

### Required fields (minimum)
Each audit event must include (as applicable):
- **event_type**: recommend | execute | rollback | override | blocked
- **timestamp_utc**
- **tenant_id / org_id** (or an internal stable identifier)
- **tenant_tier**: self_serve | enterprise | dedicated
- **residency_category**: global | us_only | eu_only | region_pinned | custom
- **primary_region**, **target_region** (target may be empty for blocked/degrade)
- **decision**: failover | degrade | stay_put
- **reason_code**: reachability | error_burn | latency_burn | capacity | manual
- **evidence_refs**: links/IDs to region health snapshots, burn-rate alert IDs, probe runs
- **actor**: automation_controller | user:<id>
- **approval_state**: not_required | pending | approved | denied
- **change_id**: routing policy config revision / feature flag revision
- **correlation_ids**: incident_id (if any), request_id samples (optional), dashboard annotation ID

### Retention and access
- Default retention (internal): **180 days** for audit events.
- Enterprise add-on / compliance packages: **≥ 400 days** retention, unless otherwise specified.
- Access must be restricted to:
  - SRE on-call and routing/control-plane engineers with an operational need
  - Security & compliance for audits and investigations
  - Customer Success only via approved exports/redactions (no raw prompt data)

### Data minimization
Audit events must not include:
- Prompt text, model outputs, embeddings, or customer payloads.
- Customer secrets (API keys, tokens).

If request samples are needed for investigation, use approved secure logging mechanisms and follow incident response data handling procedures.

## Handling of regulated / data-residency constrained customers
### If a region impairment occurs within a constrained boundary
Example: EU-only customer and eu-west is impaired.
- If eu-central is healthy and has capacity: **fail over to eu-central**.
- If no EU region is healthy/capable: **degrade within EU**.
  - Return 503 + Retry-After (preferred for overload)
  - Enforce stricter rate limits / max tokens for fairness
  - Disable non-essential optional features if supported by product policy

### Communication expectations (Enterprise)
- During a real incident: follow the Regional Failover Communication Playbook.
- For planned tests: notify only customers whose traffic might be impacted, and explicitly state that residency boundaries will not be violated.
- If any customer perceives cross-region behavior, immediately:
  - Pull audit events for the tenant
  - Validate residency gating decisions
  - Engage Security and Support escalation

## Controlled failover tests (“game days”) security requirements
Prior to production tests:
1) Confirm residency gating is active and validated in staging.
2) Explicitly exclude region-pinned and regulated tenants unless written approval is obtained.
3) Ensure audit events and dashboard annotations are functioning.
4) Validate that “blocked due to residency” is observable (metric + audit event).

During the test:
- Any attempted out-of-boundary action must be treated as a **SEV-2 security incident** if it results in data plane processing outside the boundary.

After the test:
- Export the audit event summary for the test window and attach it to the game day results doc.

## Operational checklist (on-call)
When failover automation suggests a policy change:
1) Identify tenant tier and residency category.
2) Confirm proposed target region is in allow-list.
3) Confirm automation approval requirements (some Enterprise/Dedicated tenants require ack).
4) Verify audit event emission is healthy (controller + policy engine).
5) Execute or approve.
6) If boundary prevents failover, choose degrade/stay-put path and update incident comms accordingly.

## Examples
### Example A: Enterprise EU-only tenant during us-east incident
- Primary region: us-east (should not happen for EU-only; indicates misconfiguration)
- Required action:
  - Immediately block and correct routing policy (within incident change management)
  - File Security follow-up for residency misconfiguration
  - Confirm no data plane processing occurred outside EU via audit/telemetry

### Example B: Global tenant during eu-west reachability failure
- Primary: eu-west
- Allowed: any region
- Action: fail over to us-east (or nearest healthy region by policy), emit audit events for recommend + execute + any rollback.

### Example C: Region-pinned tenant when region is impaired
- Primary: eu-west
- Allowed: eu-west only
- Action: do not fail over. Enable protective controls (circuit breakers, load shedding), return Retry-After, and communicate impact.

## Monitoring requirements (security-relevant)
Minimum dashboards/alerts needed:
- Count of `failover_blocked_due_to_residency` by tier
- Audit event delivery health (ingest lag, drop rate)
- Unauthorized/rare overrides (manual force actions)
- Drift detection: tenants with residency=EU-only receiving any non-EU routing decisions (should be zero)

## Ownership and change control
- Owner: **Security & Compliance** (in partnership with SRE Reliability)
- Routing enforcement: **Smart Routing** team (Mina Haddad) + Policy engine owner (Jordan Lee)
- Audit event pipeline: **SRE / Observability** (Allison Grant)

Changes to this document require review from:
- Security & Compliance
- SRE Reliability lead (Sean Gallagher or delegate)
- Routing policy tech lead (Ravi Menon)

## Open questions / follow-ups
- Define a standard “custom boundary” representation shared between Hosted and Dedicated policy configs.
- Confirm enterprise retention defaults for audit logs align with compliance add-ons.
- Add automated drift checks that continuously validate residency enforcement using synthetic tenant policies (no customer data).

{

    "id": "dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json",
    "title": "Runbook: Hosted API Regional Failover (On-Call)",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Runbook: Hosted API Regional Failover (On-Call)\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-sre\",\n  \"author\": \"Tom\\u00e1\\u0161 Nov\\u00e1k\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-12\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-02-10\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Rafael Mendes\",\n    \"Miles Thornton\",\n    \"Mina Haddad\",\n    \"Victor Alvarez\",\n    \"Allison Grant\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"runbook\",\n    \"hosted-api\",\n    \"failover\",\n    \"multi-region\",\n    \"sre\",\n    \"routing\",\n    \"incident-response\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"confluence://eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/regional-failover-automation-upgrade-overview\",\n    \"confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy\",\n    \"confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback\",\n    \"confluence://eng-platform/systems-and-services/region-health-service\",\n    \"confluence://eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/failover-signal-dashboards-spec\",\n    \"confluence://oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/regional-failover-communication-playbook\",\n    \"confluence://oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/status-page-template-regional-event\",\n    \"confluence://eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-pool-drain-and-evacuation-procedure\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"## Purpose\\nThis runbook describes the on-call procedure for executing (or approving) **Hosted API** regional failover during a real regional impairment or a controlled test. It covers triage, validation of trigger signals, initiating automation (including dry-run), monitoring during traffic shift, rollback, and post-event verification.\\n\\n**Primary goal:** reduce customer-visible impact by failing over quickly when the region is actually impaired, while avoiding false positives and oscillation.\\n\\n## Audience\\n- SRE On-Call (primary)\\n- Routing/Smart Routing On-Call (secondary)\\n- Network On-Call (as needed)\\n- Control Plane On-Call (as needed)\\n\\n## Definitions\\n- **Primary region:** currently preferred region for a Hosted API route/model group (e.g., `us-east` for most NA traffic).\\n- **Failover:** shifting eligible traffic from an impaired region to one or more healthy regions via routing policy updates.\\n- **Regional impairment:** region-level loss of reachability and/or sustained service-level failure (e.g., elevated 5xx burn) consistent across multiple independent signals.\\n- **Partial degradation:** single model pool, single AZ, or a dependency issue not requiring region-wide failover.\\n\\n## Preconditions / Safety\\n1) Confirm this is **Hosted API** traffic (not Dedicated-only). If Dedicated is impacted, coordinate separately per Dedicated runbooks.\\n2) Ensure you have the correct scope:\\n   - Which **route(s)**: `chat.completions`, `responses`, `embeddings`, etc.\\n   - Which **model group(s)**: `rw-llama-70b`, `rw-qwen-32b`, etc.\\n   - Which **tenant tier(s)** impacted: `free`, `pro`, `enterprise`.\\n3) Review automation mode for production:\\n   - **Dry-run** is always permitted.\\n   - **Execute** may require approval hooks depending on the route/tier configuration.\\n4) Data residency constraints: some enterprise tenants have region pinning. Failover must respect constraints (see \\u201cDo Not Fail Over\\u201d section and Security guidance).\\n\\n## Signals and Trigger Hierarchy (Summary)\\nThe authoritative prioritization is defined in **[ADR-042: Failover Trigger Signal Hierarchy]**.\\n\\nUse this simplified hierarchy when making a decision:\\n1) **Reachability loss** (cross-region probes + edge reachability) \\n2) **5xx burn-rate** for Hosted API (multi-window burn confirmation)\\n3) **Tail latency burn-rate** (P95/P99) with corroborating errors or reachability\\n4) **Capacity exhaustion / headroom collapse** (sustained) that cannot be mitigated by local scaling\\n\\n**Corroboration rule (operational):** do not execute production failover based on a single signal unless it is clearly reachability loss across multiple probe sources.\\n\\n## Required Dashboards / Links\\nRefer to **[Failover Signal Dashboards Spec]** for panel names and interpretations. Minimum set before executing:\\n- Region Health Summary (aggregated): `region-health-service` view\\n- Hosted API Availability: 2xx/4xx/5xx rate by region + route\\n- Burn-rate alerts: 5m/1h multi-window burn for multi-region availability SLO\\n- Tail latency by region: p95/p99 for key routes\\n- Capacity headroom by region: GPU queue depth, available tokens/sec, batcher saturation\\n- Routing policy flips timeline + audit events\\n- Cross-region probe results (perf-canary reachability/latency)\\n\\n## Tools\\n### Failover Controller CLI\\nUse the internal failover controller CLI to inspect, simulate, and (if permitted) execute changes.\\n\\nCommon commands (examples):\\n- Inspect current state:\\n  - `rwi-failoverctl status --service hosted-api --region us-east`\\n- Review signals / evidence:\\n  - `rwi-failoverctl evidence --service hosted-api --region us-east --window 30m`\\n- Dry-run (recommended actions only):\\n  - `rwi-failoverctl recommend --service hosted-api --from us-east --to eu-west --dry-run`\\n- Execute (requires approval hook in some prod configs):\\n  - `rwi-failoverctl execute --service hosted-api --from us-east --to eu-west --reason \\\"region impairment\\\"`\\n- Rollback:\\n  - `rwi-failoverctl rollback --service hosted-api --change-id <id> --reason \\\"region recovered\\\"`\\n\\nNotes:\\n- All dry-run and execute actions emit an audit event (see \\u201cAuditability\\u201d below).\\n- If the CLI cannot reach the controller/control plane, coordinate with Control Plane On-Call and consider manual routing policy change only as a last resort.\\n\\n### Incident-bot integration\\nThe failover controller posts summaries on trigger/recommend/execute/rollback. If missing, post manually with the template in \\u201cComms\\u201d.\\n\\n## Severity / When to Initiate Failover\\nInitiate failover actions when **either**:\\n- You see a page for regional impairment (reachability + service impact), or\\n- Multiple customers report elevated 5xx/timeouts correlated to a single region, or\\n- Burn-rate alert triggers for multi-region availability and is clearly tied to one region.\\n\\nIf impact is limited to a single route/model pool and can be mitigated locally (restart, scale, drain bad nodes), prefer local mitigation first.\\n\\n## Step-by-step Procedure\\n### 1) Triage and confirm it\\u2019s regional\\n1. Open incident channel and assign roles:\\n   - Incident Commander (IC): SRE On-Call unless escalated\\n   - Routing liaison: Smart Routing On-Call\\n   - Network liaison: Network On-Call if reachability suspected\\n   - Observability support: optional\\n2. Confirm symptoms:\\n   - Customer impact: 5xx spikes, timeouts, elevated p99, streaming disconnects\\n   - Scope: specific region (`us-east`) vs global\\n3. Check Region Health Summary:\\n   - Is `us-east` marked `DEGRADED` or `UNHEALTHY`?\\n   - Which signals contributed (reachability, 5xx burn, latency burn, capacity)?\\n4. Validate reachability:\\n   - Cross-region probes: `eu-west -> us-east`, `us-west -> us-east`\\n   - Edge reachability: client ingress success rate in region\\n   - Network indicators: packet loss, BGP/anycast anomalies (if applicable)\\n5. Validate service-level impact:\\n   - Hosted API 5xx rate by region/route\\n   - Burn-rate: confirm multi-window (fast + slow) windows are both elevated to avoid false positives\\n   - Tail latency: verify not caused solely by client retry storms\\n6. Validate capacity/headroom:\\n   - GPU pool saturation, queue depth\\n   - Autoscaler events and whether capacity can recover within minutes\\n\\nDecision checkpoint:\\n- If signals indicate **localized service issue** (single model, single AZ, single dependency), do not fail over region-wide yet. Escalate to service owner and mitigate locally.\\n- If signals indicate **region impairment**, proceed to dry-run.\\n\\n### 2) Dry-run failover recommendation (required before execute)\\n1. Run dry-run recommendation:\\n   - `rwi-failoverctl recommend --service hosted-api --from us-east --to <candidate> --dry-run`\\n2. Review output for:\\n   - Recommended destination region(s) and weights\\n   - Evidence list (signals, timestamps, confidence)\\n   - Guardrails that will apply (rate limits, hold-down timers, per-tenant safety)\\n3. Validate destination readiness:\\n   - Capacity headroom meets \\u201csafe to failover\\u201d criteria for the affected routes/models\\n   - No concurrent degradation in destination\\n   - Tail latency acceptable under projected load\\n4. Confirm \\u201cDo Not Fail Over\\u201d constraints:\\n   - Data residency pinned tenants cannot be shifted (ensure policy respects pinning)\\n   - Known incompatibilities: model version parity, feature flags, or region-specific dependencies\\n\\nIf the dry-run suggests \\u201chold / no action\\u201d due to insufficient corroboration or guardrails, do not force execute without Routing lead approval.\\n\\n### 3) Approval and execute\\nDepending on route/tier, production execute may require explicit approval.\\n\\n1. Announce intent in incident channel:\\n   - Source region, destination region(s)\\n   - Current impact (5xx/latency)\\n   - Signals justifying failover\\n   - Expected blast radius and rollback trigger\\n2. If approval hook is enabled:\\n   - Request approval from designated approver (usually SRE IC + Routing On-Call; enterprise scope may require SRE Manager)\\n3. Execute failover:\\n   - `rwi-failoverctl execute --service hosted-api --from us-east --to eu-west --reason \\\"<ticket/incident + summary>\\\"`\\n4. Confirm controller actions:\\n   - Routing policy updated\\n   - Circuit breakers / backpressure settings applied (if part of the workflow)\\n   - Audit event emitted with change-id\\n\\n### 4) Monitor during traffic shift (first 15 minutes are critical)\\nWatch these panels continuously:\\n1. Customer-visible impact:\\n   - Overall 5xx rate (global)\\n   - Route-level error rate for key endpoints\\n   - Streaming stability metrics (disconnect/reconnect)\\n2. Destination region health:\\n   - GPU queue depth / saturation\\n   - P95/P99 latency\\n   - Retry-after responses (should increase under overload rather than hard timeouts)\\n3. Failover side effects:\\n   - Thundering herd (retry spikes)\\n   - Elevated tail latency due to cache misses / cold KV cache\\n   - Unexpected auth/control-plane errors\\n\\nIf destination starts to degrade:\\n- Engage load shedding controls (per gateway defaults) and consider partial failover (reduce weights) instead of full shift.\\n- Coordinate with Routing On-Call to adjust weights or add an additional destination.\\n\\n### 5) Customer impact checks\\n1. Confirm representative customer success:\\n   - Sample synthetic requests from multiple geos\\n   - Check top enterprise tenants dashboards (if available) for elevated errors\\n2. If customer tickets are open (Support), provide:\\n   - Current status (mitigating via regional failover)\\n   - Expected behavior (brief transient errors, possible streaming reconnect)\\n   - Workaround guidance (retry with exponential backoff; honor Retry-After)\\n\\n### 6) Stabilization and decision to hold vs rollback\\nHold-down timers and anti-flap rules are defined in **[ADR-043]** and enforced by the controller. Operationally:\\n\\nRollback only when:\\n- Source region signals are healthy for the required stability window, AND\\n- Destination region is stable, AND\\n- You have a plan for a safe traffic return (gradual weights preferred)\\n\\nPrefer **gradual rollback** (weighted return) to avoid oscillation.\\n\\n### 7) Rollback procedure\\n1. Run rollback dry-run:\\n   - `rwi-failoverctl recommend --service hosted-api --from eu-west --to us-east --dry-run`\\n2. If recommended and stable, execute rollback:\\n   - `rwi-failoverctl rollback --service hosted-api --change-id <id> --reason \\\"region recovered\\\"`\\n3. Monitor for at least 30 minutes after rollback:\\n   - Error rate and latency in both regions\\n   - Policy flip rate (ensure no repeated flaps)\\n\\n## Do Not Fail Over (Common False-Positive Scenarios)\\nDo not execute a region-wide failover if the issue is likely:\\n- A single model deployment regression in-region (roll back model/version instead)\\n- Control plane impairment affecting policy distribution (failover may not apply cleanly)\\n- A global dependency outage (auth, billing, shared datastore) where failover doesn\\u2019t help\\n- Client-side retry storms causing latency (tune retries/backoff; use Retry-After)\\n- Destination region lacks sufficient headroom or is already degraded\\n- Tenant data residency pinning prevents safe cross-region routing\\n\\nWhen unsure, escalate to:\\n- Routing On-Call (policy semantics, partial failover)\\n- Network On-Call (reachability signal validation)\\n- Control Plane On-Call (controller health)\\n\\n## Auditability / Evidence Collection\\nEvery recommendation/execute/rollback should be traceable:\\n- Capture the controller change-id in the incident timeline\\n- Link dashboards used to make the decision (Region Health Summary, burn panels)\\n- Ensure audit event exists (used for enterprise audit requests)\\n\\nIf audit events are missing:\\n- Record the exact commands run and timestamps\\n- File a ticket with the failover controller team (include incident id)\\n\\n## Communication Checklist\\nFollow **[Regional Failover Communication Playbook]**.\\n\\nMinimum internal comms:\\n- Update incident channel with:\\n  - What is failing (region + symptoms)\\n  - What we did (dry-run, execute, weights)\\n  - What to watch (destination headroom, burn)\\n\\nStatus page (if customer-visible impact exceeds thresholds):\\n- Use **[Status Page Template: Regional Event]**\\n- Update cadence: every 15\\u201330 minutes while actively mitigating\\n- Ensure wording distinguishes \\u201cregional impairment\\u201d from \\u201cplanned test\\u201d\\n\\nIncident-bot manual template (if automation posts fail):\\n- \\\"Failover action: shifted Hosted API traffic from <from> to <to>. Reason: <reachability/5xx burn/latency burn/capacity>. Change-id: <id>. Monitoring: <dashboard link>. Rollback trigger: <criteria>.\\\"\\n\\n## Post-event Validation (Closeout)\\nWithin 1 hour of stabilization:\\n1. Confirm SLO impact snapshot:\\n   - Multi-region availability SLO burn during the window\\n   - Peak 5xx and duration\\n2. Confirm client experience:\\n   - Streaming reconnect metrics improved\\n   - Retry-after usage (no prolonged hard timeouts)\\n3. Confirm operational hygiene:\\n   - Controller did not flap (flip rate within limits)\\n   - Alerts returned to green and are not noisy\\n4. Create follow-ups:\\n   - Any signal gaps (missing probe, delayed burn alert)\\n   - Any dashboard gaps (missing annotations)\\n   - Any guardrails needed (rate limits, hold-down tuning)\\n\\n## Escalation / Ownership\\n- SRE On-Call: owns incident coordination and decision to execute/rollback\\n- Routing On-Call (Smart Routing): owns policy semantics, weights, constraints\\n- Network On-Call: validates reachability anomalies and provider symptoms\\n- Observability: dashboards/alert correctness\\n\\nIf repeated flapping or unclear signals occur, escalate to:\\n- Miles Thornton (Failover architecture lead)\\n- Rafael Mendes (SRE delivery lead)\\n\\n## Appendix A: Quick Validation Queries (Examples)\\nUse these as mental checklists (exact query syntax varies by dashboard):\\n- 5xx rate by region and route over last 10m vs 1h\\n- Burn-rate: fast window (5m) and slow window (1h) both elevated\\n- Cross-region probes: `success_rate < 95%` and/or latency step-change\\n- Destination headroom: sustained queue depth below alert threshold and autoscaler not maxed\\n\\n## Appendix B: Controlled Test Notes\\nFor planned game days:\\n- Always run in a limited blast radius configuration (approved tenants/routes)\\n- Announce start/end in #eng-sre and #support with explicit customer comms plan\\n- Use dry-run first, then execute with pre-agreed rollback triggers\\n- Ensure dashboards have automation annotations enabled before start\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_7373a5e70ae74cc59d6e87925ef7ffcc\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Runbook: Hosted API Regional Failover (On-Call)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-sre\n\ncontent : # # purpose this runbook describes the on - call procedure for executing ( or approving ) * * hosted api * * regional failover during a real regional impairment or a controlled test. it covers triage, validation of trigger signals, initiating automation ( including dry - run ), monitoring during traffic shift, rollback, and post - event verification. * * primary goal : * * reduce customer - visible impact by failing over quickly when the region is actually impaired, while avoiding false positives and oscillation. # # audience - sre on - call ( primary ) - routing / smart routing on - call ( secondary ) - network on - call ( as needed ) - control plane on - call ( as needed )",

  "content": "## Purpose
This runbook describes the on-call procedure for executing (or approving) **Hosted API** regional failover during a real regional impairment or a controlled test. It covers triage, validation of trigger signals, initiating automation (including dry-run), monitoring during traffic shift, rollback, and post-event verification.

**Primary goal:** reduce customer-visible impact by failing over quickly when the region is actually impaired, while avoiding false positives and oscillation.

## Audience
- SRE On-Call (primary)
- Routing/Smart Routing On-Call (secondary)
- Network On-Call (as needed)
- Control Plane On-Call (as needed)

## Definitions
- **Primary region:** currently preferred region for a Hosted API route/model group (e.g., `us-east` for most NA traffic).
- **Failover:** shifting eligible traffic from an impaired region to one or more healthy regions via routing policy updates.
- **Regional impairment:** region-level loss of reachability and/or sustained service-level failure (e.g., elevated 5xx burn) consistent across multiple independent signals.
- **Partial degradation:** single model pool, single AZ, or a dependency issue not requiring region-wide failover.

## Preconditions / Safety
1) Confirm this is **Hosted API** traffic (not Dedicated-only). If Dedicated is impacted, coordinate separately per Dedicated runbooks.
2) Ensure you have the correct scope:
   - Which **route(s)**: `chat.completions`, `responses`, `embeddings`, etc.
   - Which **model group(s)**: `rw-llama-70b`, `rw-qwen-32b`, etc.
   - Which **tenant tier(s)** impacted: `free`, `pro`, `enterprise`.
3) Review automation mode for production:
   - **Dry-run** is always permitted.
   - **Execute** may require approval hooks depending on the route/tier configuration.
4) Data residency constraints: some enterprise tenants have region pinning. Failover must respect constraints (see “Do Not Fail Over” section and Security guidance).

## Signals and Trigger Hierarchy (Summary)
The authoritative prioritization is defined in **[ADR-042: Failover Trigger Signal Hierarchy]**.

Use this simplified hierarchy when making a decision:
1) **Reachability loss** (cross-region probes + edge reachability) 
2) **5xx burn-rate** for Hosted API (multi-window burn confirmation)
3) **Tail latency burn-rate** (P95/P99) with corroborating errors or reachability
4) **Capacity exhaustion / headroom collapse** (sustained) that cannot be mitigated by local scaling

**Corroboration rule (operational):** do not execute production failover based on a single signal unless it is clearly reachability loss across multiple probe sources.

## Required Dashboards / Links
Refer to **[Failover Signal Dashboards Spec]** for panel names and interpretations. Minimum set before executing:
- Region Health Summary (aggregated): `region-health-service` view
- Hosted API Availability: 2xx/4xx/5xx rate by region + route
- Burn-rate alerts: 5m/1h multi-window burn for multi-region availability SLO
- Tail latency by region: p95/p99 for key routes
- Capacity headroom by region: GPU queue depth, available tokens/sec, batcher saturation
- Routing policy flips timeline + audit events
- Cross-region probe results (perf-canary reachability/latency)

## Tools
### Failover Controller CLI
Use the internal failover controller CLI to inspect, simulate, and (if permitted) execute changes.

Common commands (examples):
- Inspect current state:
  - `rwi-failoverctl status --service hosted-api --region us-east`
- Review signals / evidence:
  - `rwi-failoverctl evidence --service hosted-api --region us-east --window 30m`
- Dry-run (recommended actions only):
  - `rwi-failoverctl recommend --service hosted-api --from us-east --to eu-west --dry-run`
- Execute (requires approval hook in some prod configs):
  - `rwi-failoverctl execute --service hosted-api --from us-east --to eu-west --reason "region impairment"`
- Rollback:
  - `rwi-failoverctl rollback --service hosted-api --change-id <id> --reason "region recovered"`

Notes:
- All dry-run and execute actions emit an audit event (see “Auditability” below).
- If the CLI cannot reach the controller/control plane, coordinate with Control Plane On-Call and consider manual routing policy change only as a last resort.

### Incident-bot integration
The failover controller posts summaries on trigger/recommend/execute/rollback. If missing, post manually with the template in “Comms”.

## Severity / When to Initiate Failover
Initiate failover actions when **either**:
- You see a page for regional impairment (reachability + service impact), or
- Multiple customers report elevated 5xx/timeouts correlated to a single region, or
- Burn-rate alert triggers for multi-region availability and is clearly tied to one region.

If impact is limited to a single route/model pool and can be mitigated locally (restart, scale, drain bad nodes), prefer local mitigation first.

## Step-by-step Procedure
### 1) Triage and confirm it’s regional
1. Open incident channel and assign roles:
   - Incident Commander (IC): SRE On-Call unless escalated
   - Routing liaison: Smart Routing On-Call
   - Network liaison: Network On-Call if reachability suspected
   - Observability support: optional
2. Confirm symptoms:
   - Customer impact: 5xx spikes, timeouts, elevated p99, streaming disconnects
   - Scope: specific region (`us-east`) vs global
3. Check Region Health Summary:
   - Is `us-east` marked `DEGRADED` or `UNHEALTHY`?
   - Which signals contributed (reachability, 5xx burn, latency burn, capacity)?
4. Validate reachability:
   - Cross-region probes: `eu-west -> us-east`, `us-west -> us-east`
   - Edge reachability: client ingress success rate in region
   - Network indicators: packet loss, BGP/anycast anomalies (if applicable)
5. Validate service-level impact:
   - Hosted API 5xx rate by region/route
   - Burn-rate: confirm multi-window (fast + slow) windows are both elevated to avoid false positives
   - Tail latency: verify not caused solely by client retry storms
6. Validate capacity/headroom:
   - GPU pool saturation, queue depth
   - Autoscaler events and whether capacity can recover within minutes

Decision checkpoint:
- If signals indicate **localized service issue** (single model, single AZ, single dependency), do not fail over region-wide yet. Escalate to service owner and mitigate locally.
- If signals indicate **region impairment**, proceed to dry-run.

### 2) Dry-run failover recommendation (required before execute)
1. Run dry-run recommendation:
   - `rwi-failoverctl recommend --service hosted-api --from us-east --to <candidate> --dry-run`
2. Review output for:
   - Recommended destination region(s) and weights
   - Evidence list (signals, timestamps, confidence)
   - Guardrails that will apply (rate limits, hold-down timers, per-tenant safety)
3. Validate destination readiness:
   - Capacity headroom meets “safe to failover” criteria for the affected routes/models
   - No concurrent degradation in destination
   - Tail latency acceptable under projected load
4. Confirm “Do Not Fail Over” constraints:
   - Data residency pinned tenants cannot be shifted (ensure policy respects pinning)
   - Known incompatibilities: model version parity, feature flags, or region-specific dependencies

If the dry-run suggests “hold / no action” due to insufficient corroboration or guardrails, do not force execute without Routing lead approval.

### 3) Approval and execute
Depending on route/tier, production execute may require explicit approval.

1. Announce intent in incident channel:
   - Source region, destination region(s)
   - Current impact (5xx/latency)
   - Signals justifying failover
   - Expected blast radius and rollback trigger
2. If approval hook is enabled:
   - Request approval from designated approver (usually SRE IC + Routing On-Call; enterprise scope may require SRE Manager)
3. Execute failover:
   - `rwi-failoverctl execute --service hosted-api --from us-east --to eu-west --reason "<ticket/incident + summary>"`
4. Confirm controller actions:
   - Routing policy updated
   - Circuit breakers / backpressure settings applied (if part of the workflow)
   - Audit event emitted with change-id

### 4) Monitor during traffic shift (first 15 minutes are critical)
Watch these panels continuously:
1. Customer-visible impact:
   - Overall 5xx rate (global)
   - Route-level error rate for key endpoints
   - Streaming stability metrics (disconnect/reconnect)
2. Destination region health:
   - GPU queue depth / saturation
   - P95/P99 latency
   - Retry-after responses (should increase under overload rather than hard timeouts)
3. Failover side effects:
   - Thundering herd (retry spikes)
   - Elevated tail latency due to cache misses / cold KV cache
   - Unexpected auth/control-plane errors

If destination starts to degrade:
- Engage load shedding controls (per gateway defaults) and consider partial failover (reduce weights) instead of full shift.
- Coordinate with Routing On-Call to adjust weights or add an additional destination.

### 5) Customer impact checks
1. Confirm representative customer success:
   - Sample synthetic requests from multiple geos
   - Check top enterprise tenants dashboards (if available) for elevated errors
2. If customer tickets are open (Support), provide:
   - Current status (mitigating via regional failover)
   - Expected behavior (brief transient errors, possible streaming reconnect)
   - Workaround guidance (retry with exponential backoff; honor Retry-After)

### 6) Stabilization and decision to hold vs rollback
Hold-down timers and anti-flap rules are defined in **[ADR-043]** and enforced by the controller. Operationally:

Rollback only when:
- Source region signals are healthy for the required stability window, AND
- Destination region is stable, AND
- You have a plan for a safe traffic return (gradual weights preferred)

Prefer **gradual rollback** (weighted return) to avoid oscillation.

### 7) Rollback procedure
1. Run rollback dry-run:
   - `rwi-failoverctl recommend --service hosted-api --from eu-west --to us-east --dry-run`
2. If recommended and stable, execute rollback:
   - `rwi-failoverctl rollback --service hosted-api --change-id <id> --reason "region recovered"`
3. Monitor for at least 30 minutes after rollback:
   - Error rate and latency in both regions
   - Policy flip rate (ensure no repeated flaps)

## Do Not Fail Over (Common False-Positive Scenarios)
Do not execute a region-wide failover if the issue is likely:
- A single model deployment regression in-region (roll back model/version instead)
- Control plane impairment affecting policy distribution (failover may not apply cleanly)
- A global dependency outage (auth, billing, shared datastore) where failover doesn’t help
- Client-side retry storms causing latency (tune retries/backoff; use Retry-After)
- Destination region lacks sufficient headroom or is already degraded
- Tenant data residency pinning prevents safe cross-region routing

When unsure, escalate to:
- Routing On-Call (policy semantics, partial failover)
- Network On-Call (reachability signal validation)
- Control Plane On-Call (controller health)

## Auditability / Evidence Collection
Every recommendation/execute/rollback should be traceable:
- Capture the controller change-id in the incident timeline
- Link dashboards used to make the decision (Region Health Summary, burn panels)
- Ensure audit event exists (used for enterprise audit requests)

If audit events are missing:
- Record the exact commands run and timestamps
- File a ticket with the failover controller team (include incident id)

## Communication Checklist
Follow **[Regional Failover Communication Playbook]**.

Minimum internal comms:
- Update incident channel with:
  - What is failing (region + symptoms)
  - What we did (dry-run, execute, weights)
  - What to watch (destination headroom, burn)

Status page (if customer-visible impact exceeds thresholds):
- Use **[Status Page Template: Regional Event]**
- Update cadence: every 15–30 minutes while actively mitigating
- Ensure wording distinguishes “regional impairment” from “planned test”

Incident-bot manual template (if automation posts fail):
- "Failover action: shifted Hosted API traffic from <from> to <to>. Reason: <reachability/5xx burn/latency burn/capacity>. Change-id: <id>. Monitoring: <dashboard link>. Rollback trigger: <criteria>."

## Post-event Validation (Closeout)
Within 1 hour of stabilization:
1. Confirm SLO impact snapshot:
   - Multi-region availability SLO burn during the window
   - Peak 5xx and duration
2. Confirm client experience:
   - Streaming reconnect metrics improved
   - Retry-after usage (no prolonged hard timeouts)
3. Confirm operational hygiene:
   - Controller did not flap (flip rate within limits)
   - Alerts returned to green and are not noisy
4. Create follow-ups:
   - Any signal gaps (missing probe, delayed burn alert)
   - Any dashboard gaps (missing annotations)
   - Any guardrails needed (rate limits, hold-down tuning)

## Escalation / Ownership
- SRE On-Call: owns incident coordination and decision to execute/rollback
- Routing On-Call (Smart Routing): owns policy semantics, weights, constraints
- Network On-Call: validates reachability anomalies and provider symptoms
- Observability: dashboards/alert correctness

If repeated flapping or unclear signals occur, escalate to:
- Miles Thornton (Failover architecture lead)
- Rafael Mendes (SRE delivery lead)

## Appendix A: Quick Validation Queries (Examples)
Use these as mental checklists (exact query syntax varies by dashboard):
- 5xx rate by region and route over last 10m vs 1h
- Burn-rate: fast window (5m) and slow window (1h) both elevated
- Cross-region probes: `success_rate < 95%` and/or latency step-change
- Destination headroom: sustained queue depth below alert threshold and autoscaler not maxed

## Appendix B: Controlled Test Notes
For planned game days:
- Always run in a limited blast radius configuration (approved tenants/routes)
- Announce start/end in #eng-sre and #support with explicit customer comms plan
- Use dry-run first, then execute with pre-agreed rollback triggers
- Ensure dashboards have automation annotations enabled before start

    "content": "{
  "title": "Regional Failover Communication Playbook (Hosted API + Dedicated)",
  "space": "oncall-and-incident-response",
  "author": "Owen Phillips",
  "owner_team": "customer-success",
  "status": "published",

    "confluence://eng-sre/runbooks/hosted-api-regional-failover-runbook",
    "confluence://eng-platform/runbooks/routing-policy-failover-controller-runbook",
    "confluence://eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-pool-drain-and-evacuation-procedure",
    "confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-042-failover-trigger-signal-hierarchy",
    "confluence://architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-043-automated-routing-policy-rollback",

  ],
  "content": "## Purpose\nThis playbook standardizes *who says what, where, and when* during a **regional impairment** or **regional failover** affecting Redwood Inference\u2019s Hosted API and/or Dedicated capacity.\n\nIt is designed for:\n- **SRE / Incident Commander (IC):** to drive internal coordination and ensure externally visible updates are consistent and timely.\n- **Support / CS (Customer Success):** to respond to inbound questions with approved language and the right level of detail.\n- **Product / Comms approvers:** to review customer-facing statements (status page + proactive outreach) for clarity and promise discipline.\n\n## Scope\n**In-scope events**\n- Any *suspected or confirmed* regional impairment (e.g., elevated 5xx, sustained tail latency burn, network reachability failures) that may trigger or has triggered **traffic steering / failover**.\n- **Automation-driven failover actions** (including dry-run output when it materially changes operator decisions).\n- **Dedicated pool drain/evacuation** that impacts throughput or latency for a customer, even if Hosted API is unaffected.\n\n**Out of scope**\n- Customer-specific Private deployment incidents (follow Private runbooks and account-specific comms paths).\n\n## Definitions (use consistent terms)\n- **Regional impairment:** A measurable degradation in a cloud region impacting availability and/or latency (partial or full).\n- **Failover:** Routing traffic away from an impaired primary region to an alternate region (temporary or sustained).\n- **Traffic steering:** Any routing policy change that shifts traffic (includes partial shifts, per-route changes).\n- **Customer impact:** A user-visible error rate increase, timeouts, degraded streaming stability, or significant latency increase relative to SLO.\n\n## Roles & approvals\n### Incident roles (comms-specific)\n- **Incident Commander (IC):** typically SRE on-call. Owns the overall incident timeline, severity, and internal/external coordination.\n- **Comms Lead:** usually **Support Incident Liaison** (primary) or **CS** (secondary). Owns wording, cadence, and customer targeting.\n- **Status Page Publisher:** individual with status page permissions (often Comms Lead or on-call Support lead).\n- **Approver(s):** required approvers for customer-facing updates depending on severity (see matrix below).\n\n### Approval matrix\n| Severity / Scenario | Status page update required | Approval required before first external update | Notes |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| SEV-1 (multi-tenant, broad availability impact) | Yes | IC + Support Lead (Dev Patel) + Product (Nikhil Sharma for Hosted / Lauren Bishop for Dedicated) | For major events, loop VP/Director SRE if time allows, but do not block first update. |\n| SEV-2 (limited impact, sustained burn, automation failover executed) | Usually yes | IC + Support Lead | Product review recommended for follow-up language. |\n| SEV-3 (minor degradation, no customer impact confirmed yet) | Not usually | IC | Prefer internal-only update and prepare draft. |\n| Planned controlled failover test (game day) | Yes (planned maintenance / test notice) | Reliability Program Lead (Sean Gallagher) + Support Lead | Use \u201cplanned test\u201d templates; do not describe as outage. |\n\n**Always involve Security & Compliance** if:\n- There is a credible risk of **data residency** boundary issues, or\n- A customer alleges cross-region routing violated contractual terms, or\n- The incident involves key management/audit log anomalies.\n\nEscalation contact (security/compliance): follow *Failover and Security Boundaries* page and page the Security on-call.\n\n## Communication objectives\n1) **Accuracy over completeness:** state what we know, what we\u2019re doing, and when we\u2019ll update next.\n2) **Promise discipline:** avoid committing to specific ETAs unless high confidence.\n3) **Consistency:** Support replies, status page, and internal incident timeline must match.\n4) **Customer trust:** explain mitigations (traffic steering, capacity scaling, retries/backoff guidance) without exposing sensitive infrastructure details.\n5) **Minimize churn in messaging:** updates should be meaningful; don\u2019t publish frequent micro-edits.\n\n## Where to communicate (channels)\n### Internal channels (default)\n- **Slack #incidents** (or incident-specific channel): canonical operational coordination.\n- **Slack #eng-sre**: SRE coordination and paging follow-ups.\n- **Slack #support**: Support/CS coordination; post approved language here.\n- **Incident-bot timeline:** ensure key milestones are recorded (start time, symptoms, failover action, stabilization, resolution).\n\n### External channels\n- **Status page:** primary external broadcast mechanism.\n- **Proactive customer outreach:** email to selected enterprise accounts (especially Dedicated and regulated customers) when there is credible impact or planned tests.\n- **Support tickets (inbound):** respond with approved language; link to status page.\n\n## Standard cadence\n### For unplanned regional impairment\n- **T+0\u201310 min:** Internal incident declared (SEV assessed). Assign Comms Lead.\n- **T+10\u201320 min:** First external status page update if impact is confirmed or highly likely.\n- **Every 30 min** (SEV-1) or **every 60 min** (SEV-2): update status page (even if \u201cno change\u201d).\n- **After mitigation / failover action:** update within 10\u201315 min to reflect change and what customers should expect.\n- **Resolution:** update when metrics stabilize and rollback/hold-down decisions are clear; follow with a final \u201cmonitoring\u201d note if needed.\n\n### For planned controlled failover tests\n- **T-3 to T-5 business days:** targeted proactive outreach to impacted enterprise accounts (if any), including what to expect.\n- **T-24 hours:** status page \u201cplanned test\u201d notice.\n- **T-15 min:** internal reminder + ensure Support macros are ready.\n- **During test:** status page update at start + at completion; optionally mid-test if customer-visible anomalies occur.\n\n## Decision tree: do we post externally?\nPost an external update (status page) if **any** are true:\n- Sustained **availability SLO burn** in a region impacting customer requests.\n- Failover/traffic steering is executed or likely.\n- Dedicated drain/evacuation is initiated for a customer and may reduce throughput.\n- Support receives multiple independent customer reports consistent with a region event.\n\nDo **not** post externally (yet) if **all** are true:\n- Signals are isolated to a single service component with no customer impact.\n- Investigation indicates false-positive triggers (e.g., one probe source down) and the IC believes it will resolve quickly.\n- No failover or customer-visible degradation is expected.\n\nWhen uncertain: prepare draft language and get IC approval; bias toward transparency if impact is plausible.\n\n## Message content guidelines\n### Use this structure\n1) **What\u2019s happening:** symptom and affected region(s).\n2) **Customer impact:** error rates/timeouts/latency/streaming stability, and which products (Hosted vs Dedicated).\n3) **What we\u2019re doing:** mitigation actions (e.g., routing traffic, increasing capacity, investigating provider networking).\n4) **What customers should do (if anything):** retry guidance, backoff, idempotency best practices for streaming reconnect.\n5) **Next update time.**\n\n### Avoid\n- Speculating on root cause before confirmation.\n- Overly detailed infra disclosures (specific GPU counts, internal hostnames, cloud tickets).\n- Blaming external providers in early updates.\n- Saying \u201cresolved\u201d while failover is still in effect and metrics are unstable.\n\n## Status page templates\n> Notes:\n> - Replace bracketed fields.\n> - Keep the first update short; add detail in follow-ups.\n> - Always include **time of next update**.\n\n### Template A \u2014 Investigating (unplanned)\n**Title:** Investigating elevated errors/latency in [REGION]\n\n**Body:**\nWe are investigating reports of elevated error rates and increased latency for requests served from **[REGION]**. Some customers may see **timeouts**, **5xx errors**, and/or **degraded streaming stability**.\n\nWe are actively investigating and preparing mitigations, including traffic steering to alternate regions where appropriate.\n\nNext update by **[TIME + 30\u201360m]**.\n\n### Template B \u2014 Mitigating / Failover in progress\n**Title:** Mitigating regional impairment in [REGION] (traffic steering in progress)\n\n**Body:**\nWe have identified a regional impairment affecting **[REGION]**. We are **steering traffic** to alternate regions to reduce customer impact.\n\nSome customers may experience transient errors during the routing transition. If you see failures, please **retry with exponential backoff**. For streaming requests, clients should be prepared to **reconnect** and resume idempotently.\n\nWe are monitoring error rates, latency, and capacity in the destination regions.\n\nNext update by **[TIME]**.\n\n### Template C \u2014 Monitoring (stabilized under failover)\n**Title:** Monitoring after mitigation for [REGION]\n\n**Body:**\nMitigations are in place and customer-facing metrics have improved. Traffic steering remains active while we continue monitoring stability and confirming safe rollback conditions.\n\nNext update by **[TIME]**.\n\n### Template D \u2014 Resolved\n**Title:** Resolved: regional impairment in [REGION]\n\n**Body:**\nThis incident is resolved. Error rates and latency have returned to normal levels.\n\nIf you continue to see issues, please contact Support and reference this status page event.\n\n### Template E \u2014 Planned controlled failover test\n**Title:** Planned controlled failover test (traffic steering) \u2014 [DATE/TIME WINDOW] UTC\n\n**Body:**\nWe will conduct a **planned controlled failover test** during **[WINDOW]** to validate regional resiliency and reduce customer impact during future incidents.\n\nDuring this test, some customers may observe brief transient errors or reconnects as traffic is steered between regions. We will monitor closely and roll back immediately if success criteria are not met.\n\nWe will post updates here at the start and end of the test.\n\n## Support/CS response macros (approved language)\n### Macro 1 \u2014 Customer reports 5xx/timeouts (unplanned)\nThanks for the report. We\u2019re currently investigating a regional issue that may be causing elevated errors/timeouts. We\u2019re applying mitigations, including traffic steering, and tracking updates on our status page here: [STATUS_PAGE_LINK].\n\nIf you can share:\n- approximate timestamps (with timezone),\n- request IDs (if available), and\n- affected model/route,\nwe can correlate with our telemetry.\n\n### Macro 2 \u2014 Streaming disconnects during failover\nDuring regional traffic steering, some streaming connections can be interrupted while routing transitions. Recommended client behavior is to reconnect and retry with backoff, using idempotency controls where possible.\n\nWe\u2019re actively monitoring stability and will post updates on the status page: [STATUS_PAGE_LINK].\n\n### Macro 3 \u2014 Dedicated customer asks about drain/failover\nWe may temporarily steer traffic and/or drain capacity to protect service availability during a regional impairment. We aim to minimize disruption and will communicate any expected impact and changes in routing status.\n\nFor your account specifically, we can confirm the affected region(s), mitigation status, and whether any traffic steering is active. Please share a timeframe and any request IDs so we can validate against our logs.\n\n## Proactive outreach: who to notify\n### When to proactively notify enterprise customers\nProactively notify (email) when **any** are true:\n- SEV-1 or SEV-2 with >15 minutes confirmed impact.\n- Dedicated customers are affected (throughput reduction, drain event, or sustained tail latency).\n- Regulated customers may have questions about residency boundaries (even if we did not cross them).\n- Planned controlled failover test that could cause visible transient errors.\n\n### Targeting guidance\n- **Dedicated:** Always include the account owner (CSM) and the customer\u2019s primary on-call contact if provided.\n- **Hosted API enterprise tiers:** Notify only if there is measurable impact or repeated customer reports.\n- **Self-serve / PLG:** status page + Support macros are typically sufficient.\n\n## Escalation paths\n### Internal escalation\n- **IC / SRE:** page SRE secondary if investigation is not converging in 15 minutes or if failover automation behaves unexpectedly.\n- **Routing/Policy:** page Routing on-call / policy engine owner if traffic steering decisions are unclear or oscillating.\n- **Infra/Networking:** page Network (Victor Alvarez) if reachability probes show cross-region path anomalies.\n- **Support:** escalate to Support Lead (Dev Patel) for coordinated customer messaging and ticket triage.\n- **Product:** loop Hosted API PM (Nikhil Sharma) / Dedicated PM (Lauren Bishop) for high-visibility accounts or repeated external inquiries.\n\n### Customer escalation\n- If a customer claims breach of data residency / contractual routing constraints:\n  1) Acknowledge and pause speculation.\n  2) Escalate immediately to Security & Compliance on-call.\n  3) Coordinate with IC before any further customer statement.\n\n## Required internal artifacts (for consistency)\nThe Comms Lead must ensure the following are updated during the event:\n- Incident channel has a pinned **current customer-facing statement**.\n- Status page updates are linked in the incident timeline.\n- Incident-bot summaries (if posted) match status page wording (no conflicting metrics).\n- A short \u201cSupport summary\u201d is posted in #support after each status page update.\n\n## Checklist (Comms Lead)\n1) Confirm severity + scope with IC (Hosted, Dedicated, or both).\n2) Draft first status page update using Template A or B.\n3) Get approvals per matrix (do not block on non-required approvals).\n4) Publish status page update; post link + text in incident channel and #support.\n5) Prepare Support macro snippet for inbound tickets.\n6) For Dedicated: confirm if any drains/evacuations are active; if yes, align language with Infra lead.\n7) Maintain cadence; update timestamps and \u201cnext update\u201d time.\n8) On resolution: publish final update; capture customer-facing summary for postmortem.\n\n## Post-incident communication\n- For SEV-1 events, provide a short customer-facing summary within **2 business days** (via status page post-incident note or targeted email), coordinated by Support Lead + Product.\n- Do not include sensitive internal details; focus on customer impact, mitigations, and prevention themes.\n- Ensure internal postmortem links are not shared externally.\n\n## FAQ / common questions (approved answers)\n**Q: Did you fail over my traffic to another region?**\nA: During regional impairments we may steer traffic to alternate regions to reduce errors and downtime. We can confirm whether traffic steering was active for your account and which regions were involved. Please share a timeframe and request IDs.\n\n**Q: Will my data leave its configured region?**\nA: For customers with data residency constraints, we apply routing boundaries and do not steer traffic across restricted regions. If you have specific residency requirements, we can review your configuration and confirm what boundaries are in effect for your account.\n\n**Q: Why did I see brief spikes during mitigation?**\nA: During traffic steering, clients may experience transient errors while routes converge and capacity stabilizes. Retries with exponential backoff typically succeed quickly. We also tune circuit breakers and overload handling to reduce repeated failures.\n\n---\n## Owner & maintenance\n**Owner team:** Customer Success (Support Incident Liaison), in partnership with SRE.\n\n**Maintenance cadence:** Review quarterly and after each controlled failover game day. Update templates when status page standards or failover automation behavior changes.\n\n**Primary contacts:**\n- Reliability program lead: Sean Gallagher\n- SRE delivery lead: Rafael Mendes\n- Support escalation owner: Dev Patel\n- Support incident liaison: Owen Phillips\n",
