    "title": "Security review escalation and handoff (CS/Support playbook)",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Security review escalation and handoff (CS/Support playbook)\",\n  \"space\": \"customer-success-and-support\",\n  \"author\": \"Jasmine Liu\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"customer-success\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-11-18\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-02-21\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Dr. Aisha Rahman\",\n    \"Olga Petrov\",\n    \"Daniel Carter\",\n    \"Marcus Lin\",\n    \"Naomi Feldman\",\n    \"Markus Klein\",\n    \"Stephanie Nguyen\",\n    \"Rachel Kim\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"security-review\",\n    \"escalation\",\n    \"soc2\",\n    \"evidence\",\n    \"rfp\",\n    \"handoff\",\n    \"support\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"confluence://sales-enablement/security-faq/redwood-enterprise-security-faq-2026\",\n    \"confluence://security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/soc2-customer-evidence-request-playbook\",\n    \"confluence://finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/rfp-response-ownership-and-approvals\",\n    \"confluence://security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions/customer-security-questionnaire-exceptions-policy\",\n    \"confluence://security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/sso-saml-scim-and-rbac-capabilities\",\n    \"confluence://security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-logging-customer-overview\",\n    \"confluence://security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/customer-facing-data-retention-and-deletion-overview\",\n    \"confluence://sales-enablement/security-faq/standard-answers-sso-rbac-audit-logs\"\n  ],\n  \"content\": \"## Purpose\\nThis playbook defines how Customer Success (CS) and Support partner with Sales, Solutions Engineering (SE), and Security/GRC during late-stage security reviews. It standardizes:\\n- When and how to loop in Security/GRC\\n- How to handle urgent deadlines and incomplete questionnaires\\n- Escalation tiers, response SLAs, and handoff points\\n- How we avoid unapproved claims and keep a clear audit trail\\n\\nThis is an internal operating document. It references restricted evidence processes (e.g., SOC 2 report) but does not include restricted artifacts.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## When to use this playbook\\nUse this playbook when any of the following occur:\\n- A prospect/customer requests SOC 2 report, pen test summary, subprocessor list, or other formal evidence.\\n- A prospect/customer sends a security questionnaire, RFP security section, or needs a security addendum.\\n- Procurement/security introduces a hard deadline (\\\\<= 5 business days) or threatens deal delay without answers.\\n- The customer requires deployment-specific assurances (Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted) around data flows, retention, encryption, KMS, logging, SSO/RBAC, or incident notification.\\n\\nNot in scope:\\n- Product roadmap commitments or \\u201ccustom features\\u201d to satisfy a questionnaire. Use the Exceptions Policy for non-supported controls.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Roles and responsibilities (who does what)\\n### Primary owners\\n- Sales / AE: owns customer timeline, coordinates meetings, maintains CRM notes, ensures customer has correct links.\\n- Solutions Engineering (SE): owns technical narrative (deployment mode, architecture diagrams, controls explanations).\\n- Security Engineering: validates technical claims, clarifies implementation details, reviews non-standard security language.\\n- GRC (Governance, Risk, Compliance): owns audit/compliance language and evidence distribution process (SOC 2 under NDA, artifact lists, timelines).\\n- Legal: owns contractual language (DPA, security addendum, breach notification terms).\\n- CS / Support: owns the escalation workflow, ensures correct process is followed, prevents churn/relationship damage, and creates a clean handoff to post-close operations.\\n\\n### CS/Support \\u201csingle-threaded owner\\u201d (STO)\\nFor any security review that is time-bound or involves evidence requests, CS/Support assigns a single-threaded owner who:\\n- Creates/updates the tracking ticket(s)\\n- Confirms next steps and internal owners\\n- Drives SLA compliance and escalations\\n- Ensures final approved language is used\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Golden rules (do / don\\u2019t)\\n### Do\\n- Use the published Security FAQ and standard answer blocks as the starting point.\\n- Confirm the customer\\u2019s deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) before answering.\\n- Route formal evidence requests through the Evidence Request Playbook (NDA checks, controlled distribution).\\n- Track all customer asks, versions, and approvals in a ticket and in CRM.\\n\\n### Don\\u2019t\\n- Don\\u2019t claim certifications we do not have (e.g., \\u201cISO 27001 certified\\u201d) or imply \\u201ccompliant with X\\u201d unless approved.\\n- Don\\u2019t promise data residency beyond what is available in the customer\\u2019s selected region/deployment mode.\\n- Don\\u2019t share restricted evidence (SOC 2 report, pen test summary) over email or Slack without following the controlled process.\\n- Don\\u2019t edit standard RFP/security language \\u201cjust to make it fit.\\u201d Use the approval workflow.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Intake checklist (required information before escalating)\\nCS/Support STO should collect the following before pulling in Security/GRC:\\n1) Account + deal context\\n- Customer/prospect name, segment, region\\n- Stage (evaluation, procurement, renewal, expansion)\\n- Business impact and date the deal will stall without response\\n\\n2) Deployment mode and architecture\\n- Hosted API / Dedicated / Private (VPC or on-prem)\\n- Target cloud/region(s) and any data residency constraints\\n- Any special requirements (HIPAA/BAA request, financial services controls, air-gapped constraints)\\n\\n3) Customer asks (exact wording)\\n- Questionnaire/RFP sections pasted verbatim or attached\\n- Specific artifacts requested (SOC 2, policies, subprocessor list, pen test summary)\\n- Required response format and due date/time zone\\n\\n4) Constraints\\n- NDA status (executed? pending? required?)\\n- Customer\\u2019s requested response channel (portal, email, GRC tool)\\n- Any customer \\u201cred lines\\u201d (e.g., retention must be configurable to X days)\\n\\n5) Internal context\\n- Existing approved snippets used (link to FAQ section or RFP library block)\\n- Any planned deviations from standard language (must be explicitly flagged)\\n\\nIf any of the above is missing, proceed with escalation but mark as \\u201cincomplete intake\\u201d and request missing items in parallel.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Escalation tiers and SLAs\\nCS/Support uses the following tiers to set expectations and drive responsiveness.\\n\\n### P0 \\u2014 Imminent deadline / deal-stopping within 24 hours\\nCriteria:\\n- Customer deadline in \\\\<= 1 business day OR live procurement call requiring answers\\n- Customer requires evidence distribution (SOC 2) to proceed immediately\\n\\nSLA targets:\\n- Acknowledge internally within 30 minutes (business hours)\\n- First response plan within 2 hours\\n\\nApprovals:\\n- Any non-standard claim requires Security + GRC approval (and Legal if contractual)\\n\\n### P1 \\u2014 Time-bound security review (2\\u20135 business days)\\nCriteria:\\n- RFP/questionnaire due in 2\\u20135 business days\\n- Customer is blocked pending \\u201csecurity sign-off\\u201d meeting\\n\\nSLA targets:\\n- Acknowledge internally within 4 business hours\\n- Draft response/plan within 1 business day\\n\\n### P2 \\u2014 Standard review (\\\\>= 6 business days)\\nCriteria:\\n- No imminent risk; customer requests information for internal review\\n\\nSLA targets:\\n- Acknowledge within 1 business day\\n- Provide materials/plan within 3 business days\\n\\nBusiness hours assumption: Mon\\u2013Fri, local team coverage. If customer is in EMEA/APAC and timing is critical, treat as one tier higher to account for time zone compression.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Step-by-step workflow (CS/Support STO)\\n### Step 1 \\u2014 Create a tracking ticket and identify the STO\\nCreate a ticket in the internal system of record (Support/Jira or the designated GTM intake queue) with:\\n- Tier (P0/P1/P2)\\n- Due date/time zone\\n- Links/attachments to the questionnaire/RFP portal\\n- Requested artifacts list\\n- Deployment mode and region\\n\\nAdd watchers:\\n- AE + SE lead on the account\\n- GRC on-call analyst (or team alias)\\n- Security Engineering reviewer (if technical claims are involved)\\n- Legal reviewer (if contract language requested)\\n\\n### Step 2 \\u2014 Send the internal \\u201cfirst plan\\u201d message\\nWithin the SLA window, post a clear plan (in the ticket and in the designated internal channel):\\n- What we will answer with standard language\\n- What requires review/approval\\n- What evidence requires NDA + controlled process\\n- Who owns each workstream and deadlines\\n\\n### Step 3 \\u2014 Separate \\u201clanguage\\u201d work from \\u201cevidence\\u201d work\\nRun two tracks in parallel:\\nA) Response language\\n- Use the Security FAQ and Standard Answers as the baseline.\\n- If the questionnaire asks for non-supported controls, use the Exceptions Policy to propose alternative language.\\n- If the customer requires a custom architecture/security narrative, SE drafts and Security validates.\\n\\nB) Evidence requests\\n- Follow the SOC 2 Customer Evidence Request Playbook.\\n- Confirm NDA status before any restricted artifact is shared.\\n- Log exactly which artifacts were shared, when, and via what method.\\n\\n### Step 4 \\u2014 Run a time-boxed review cycle\\nFor P0/P1, use a single redline pass with explicit approvers:\\n- Security Engineering: technical controls, logging, encryption, runtime behavior\\n- GRC: compliance posture wording, audit periods, \\u201creport under NDA\\u201d phrasing\\n- Legal: DPA/addendum terms, breach notification, liability language\\n\\nIf edits exceed one pass or the customer changes scope, re-baseline and reset expectations with Sales.\\n\\n### Step 5 \\u2014 Customer-facing delivery\\nCS/Support STO ensures:\\n- Final answers use approved language and correct deployment mode caveats\\n- Restricted artifacts are delivered only via the approved method\\n- The customer receives a concise \\u201cwhat we sent + how to follow up\\u201d summary\\n\\nRecommended customer email structure:\\n- One-paragraph overview\\n- Bullets of attached/linked documents\\n- Evidence request steps (if applicable)\\n- Offer a 30-minute security review call with Security/GRC if needed\\n\\n### Step 6 \\u2014 Close the loop and create post-close handoff notes\\nOnce the security review is complete (or \\u201cgood enough\\u201d for procurement), capture:\\n- Final list of commitments made (e.g., log retention option selected, region selection)\\n- Any exceptions granted and their approvers\\n- Any open items that must be implemented/configured during onboarding\\n\\nAdd the notes to CRM and to the account\\u2019s implementation plan.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Common scenarios and how to handle them\\n### Scenario A: \\u201cSend us your SOC 2 report today\\u201d\\n1) Confirm whether NDA is executed.\\n2) If NDA is not executed, coordinate with Legal/Sales immediately; do not share the report.\\n3) Use the approved wording: \\u201cSOC 2 Type II report available under NDA upon request.\\u201d\\n4) Open an evidence request per the playbook and track distribution.\\n\\n### Scenario B: Customer asks \\u201cDo you train on our data?\\u201d\\n- Use the exact FAQ language and definitions (training vs transient processing; prompts/logs vs model weights).\\n- Do not introduce new qualifiers. If customer asks for contract language, route to Legal.\\n\\n### Scenario C: EU data residency objection (must stay in EU)\\n- Confirm which regions are available for the chosen deployment mode.\\n- Use the approved residency language (no blanket promises). If constraints can only be met with Private, have SE present options.\\n- Escalate to GRC/Security if the customer requests written guarantees beyond standard documentation.\\n\\n### Scenario D: Questionnaire asks for a control we do not support (e.g., specific IdP feature, custom audit event)\\n- Do not answer \\u201cYes\\u201d with future intent.\\n- Use the Exceptions Policy to provide alternative language and document compensating controls.\\n- If customer insists on a \\u201cmust-have,\\u201d flag to Product Security PM for capability alignment (without committing roadmap).\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Communication channels and meeting guidance\\n### Internal channels (recommended)\\n- Use the designated security review intake channel and link the tracking ticket.\\n- Keep decisions in the ticket. Slack is for coordination, not for the authoritative record.\\n\\n### Customer call structure (30\\u201345 minutes)\\n1) Confirm deployment mode + region + data flow expectations\\n2) Walk through top 5 controls customer cares about (usually: data use, encryption, access controls, logging, retention)\\n3) Evidence requests: explain NDA gating and timelines\\n4) Capture remaining blockers and assign owners\\n\\nAvoid:\\n- Live \\u201coff the cuff\\u201d answers to compliance/certification questions. Offer to follow up with approved language.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Handback to CS/Support after close (operationalization)\\nIf any of the following were discussed, CS must validate configuration during onboarding:\\n- Audit log export destination (SIEM/S3) and retention window\\n- SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning requirements\\n- RBAC roles and least-privilege model for admins\\n- Data retention/deletion configuration for the chosen deployment mode\\n- Private deployment network boundaries (VPC peering, egress controls) and key management (KMS/HSM)\\n\\nCreate an onboarding checklist item for each requirement and confirm acceptance criteria with the customer security contact.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Templates\\n### Internal escalation summary (paste into ticket)\\nAccount:\\nDeployment mode:\\nRegion(s):\\nTier (P0/P1/P2):\\nCustomer deadline (date/time zone):\\nTop asks (verbatim):\\nArtifacts requested:\\nNDA status:\\nDraft response plan (what we can answer with standard language vs needs review):\\nOwners:\\n\\n### Customer follow-up email (minimal)\\nSubject: Redwood security review materials + next steps\\n\\nHi <Name>,\\n\\nSharing the requested security materials for your review:\\n- <Doc link 1>\\n- <Doc link 2>\\n- <Audit logging / retention overview>\\n\\nFor the SOC 2 Type II report (restricted), we can provide it under NDA via our controlled evidence request process. If you confirm NDA status, we will initiate distribution.\\n\\nHappy to schedule a 30-minute security review call to walk through data handling, encryption, access controls, and audit logging.\\n\\nBest,\\n<Name>\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Metrics and continuous improvement\\nCS/Support STO should log the following for quarterly review:\\n- Time-to-acknowledge and time-to-first-draft by tier\\n- # of evidence requests and average turnaround time\\n- Top repeated questionnaire questions and where our standard language was insufficient\\n- Any instances of \\u201cunapproved language\\u201d caught in review (and required remediation)\\n\\nFeedback loop:\\n- If a question repeats \\\\>= 3 times in a month, open a request to update the Security FAQ or RFP library rather than rewriting per deal.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Ownership and review cadence\\nOwner: Customer Success (CS sponsor), in partnership with Security/GRC.\\nReview cadence: Quarterly, or immediately after any material change to security posture, evidence availability, or product behavior affecting common questionnaire answers.\\n\\nLast review highlights (2026-02-21):\\n- Tightened P0/P1 SLA expectations and clarified NDA gating for evidence.\\n- Standardized separation of \\u201clanguage\\u201d vs \\u201cevidence\\u201d workstreams.\\n- Added explicit post-close operationalization checklist items (SSO/SCIM, audit logs, retention).\",\n  \"original_location\": \"confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/security-review-escalation-and-handoff.json\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"content\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_2ea8e611a8b448ffab3bc5b927a3d466\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Security review escalation and handoff (CS/Support playbook)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/security-review-escalation-and-handoff.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: customer-success-and-support\n\n# # roles and responsibilities ( who does what ) # # # primary owners - sales / ae : owns customer timeline, coordinates meetings, maintains crm notes, ensures customer has correct links. - solutions engineering ( se ) : owns technical narrative ( deployment mode, architecture diagrams, controls explanations ). - security engineering : validates technical claims, clarifies implementation details, reviews non - standard security language. - grc ( governance, risk, compliance ) : owns audit / compliance language and evidence distribution process ( soc 2 under nda, artifact lists, timelines ). - legal : owns contractual language ( dpa, security addendum, breach notification terms ). - cs / support : owns the escalation workflow, ensures correct process is followed, prevents churn / relationship damage,",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Security review escalation and handoff (CS/Support playbook)\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/security-review-escalation-and-handoff.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: customer-success-and-support\n\n- what requires review / approval - what evidence requires nda + controlled process - who owns each workstream and deadlines # # # step 3 — separate “ language ” work from “ evidence ” work run two tracks in parallel : a ) response language - use the security faq and standard answers as the baseline. - if the questionnaire asks for non - supported controls, use the exceptions policy to propose alternative language. - if the customer requires a custom architecture / security narrative, se drafts and security validates. b ) evidence requests - follow the soc 2 customer evidence request playbook. - confirm nda status before any restricted artifact is shared. - log exactly which artifacts were shared, when, and via what method.",

{
  "title": "Security review escalation and handoff (CS/Support playbook)",
  "space": "customer-success-and-support",
  "author": "Jasmine Liu",
  "owner_team": "customer-success",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2025-11-18",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-21",
  "reviewers": [
    "Dr. Aisha Rahman",
    "Olga Petrov",
    "Daniel Carter",
    "Marcus Lin",
    "Naomi Feldman",
    "Markus Klein",
    "Stephanie Nguyen",
    "Rachel Kim"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "security-review",
    "escalation",
    "soc2",
    "evidence",
    "rfp",
    "handoff",
    "support"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "related_pages": [
    "confluence://sales-enablement/security-faq/redwood-enterprise-security-faq-2026",
    "confluence://security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/soc2-customer-evidence-request-playbook",
    "confluence://finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/rfp-response-ownership-and-approvals",
    "confluence://security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions/customer-security-questionnaire-exceptions-policy",
    "confluence://security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/sso-saml-scim-and-rbac-capabilities",
    "confluence://security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-logging-customer-overview",
    "confluence://security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/customer-facing-data-retention-and-deletion-overview",
    "confluence://sales-enablement/security-faq/standard-answers-sso-rbac-audit-logs"
  ],
  "content": "## Purpose
This playbook defines how Customer Success (CS) and Support partner with Sales, Solutions Engineering (SE), and Security/GRC during late-stage security reviews. It standardizes:
- When and how to loop in Security/GRC
- How to handle urgent deadlines and incomplete questionnaires
- Escalation tiers, response SLAs, and handoff points
- How we avoid unapproved claims and keep a clear audit trail

This is an internal operating document. It references restricted evidence processes (e.g., SOC 2 report) but does not include restricted artifacts.

---

## When to use this playbook
Use this playbook when any of the following occur:
- A prospect/customer requests SOC 2 report, pen test summary, subprocessor list, or other formal evidence.
- A prospect/customer sends a security questionnaire, RFP security section, or needs a security addendum.
- Procurement/security introduces a hard deadline (\<= 5 business days) or threatens deal delay without answers.
- The customer requires deployment-specific assurances (Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted) around data flows, retention, encryption, KMS, logging, SSO/RBAC, or incident notification.

Not in scope:
- Product roadmap commitments or “custom features” to satisfy a questionnaire. Use the Exceptions Policy for non-supported controls.

---

## Roles and responsibilities (who does what)
### Primary owners
- Sales / AE: owns customer timeline, coordinates meetings, maintains CRM notes, ensures customer has correct links.
- Solutions Engineering (SE): owns technical narrative (deployment mode, architecture diagrams, controls explanations).
- Security Engineering: validates technical claims, clarifies implementation details, reviews non-standard security language.
- GRC (Governance, Risk, Compliance): owns audit/compliance language and evidence distribution process (SOC 2 under NDA, artifact lists, timelines).
- Legal: owns contractual language (DPA, security addendum, breach notification terms).
- CS / Support: owns the escalation workflow, ensures correct process is followed, prevents churn/relationship damage, and creates a clean handoff to post-close operations.

### CS/Support “single-threaded owner” (STO)
For any security review that is time-bound or involves evidence requests, CS/Support assigns a single-threaded owner who:
- Creates/updates the tracking ticket(s)
- Confirms next steps and internal owners
- Drives SLA compliance and escalations
- Ensures final approved language is used

---

## Golden rules (do / don’t)
### Do
- Use the published Security FAQ and standard answer blocks as the starting point.
- Confirm the customer’s deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) before answering.
- Route formal evidence requests through the Evidence Request Playbook (NDA checks, controlled distribution).
- Track all customer asks, versions, and approvals in a ticket and in CRM.

### Don’t
- Don’t claim certifications we do not have (e.g., “ISO 27001 certified”) or imply “compliant with X” unless approved.
- Don’t promise data residency beyond what is available in the customer’s selected region/deployment mode.
- Don’t share restricted evidence (SOC 2 report, pen test summary) over email or Slack without following the controlled process.
- Don’t edit standard RFP/security language “just to make it fit.” Use the approval workflow.

---

## Intake checklist (required information before escalating)
CS/Support STO should collect the following before pulling in Security/GRC:
1) Account + deal context
- Customer/prospect name, segment, region
- Stage (evaluation, procurement, renewal, expansion)
- Business impact and date the deal will stall without response

2) Deployment mode and architecture
- Hosted API / Dedicated / Private (VPC or on-prem)
- Target cloud/region(s) and any data residency constraints
- Any special requirements (HIPAA/BAA request, financial services controls, air-gapped constraints)

3) Customer asks (exact wording)
- Questionnaire/RFP sections pasted verbatim or attached
- Specific artifacts requested (SOC 2, policies, subprocessor list, pen test summary)
- Required response format and due date/time zone

4) Constraints
- NDA status (executed? pending? required?)
- Customer’s requested response channel (portal, email, GRC tool)
- Any customer “red lines” (e.g., retention must be configurable to X days)

5) Internal context
- Existing approved snippets used (link to FAQ section or RFP library block)
- Any planned deviations from standard language (must be explicitly flagged)

If any of the above is missing, proceed with escalation but mark as “incomplete intake” and request missing items in parallel.

---

## Escalation tiers and SLAs
CS/Support uses the following tiers to set expectations and drive responsiveness.

### P0 — Imminent deadline / deal-stopping within 24 hours
Criteria:
- Customer deadline in \<= 1 business day OR live procurement call requiring answers
- Customer requires evidence distribution (SOC 2) to proceed immediately

SLA targets:
- Acknowledge internally within 30 minutes (business hours)
- First response plan within 2 hours

Approvals:
- Any non-standard claim requires Security + GRC approval (and Legal if contractual)

### P1 — Time-bound security review (2–5 business days)
Criteria:
- RFP/questionnaire due in 2–5 business days
- Customer is blocked pending “security sign-off” meeting

SLA targets:
- Acknowledge internally within 4 business hours
- Draft response/plan within 1 business day

### P2 — Standard review (\>= 6 business days)
Criteria:
- No imminent risk; customer requests information for internal review

SLA targets:
- Acknowledge within 1 business day
- Provide materials/plan within 3 business days

Business hours assumption: Mon–Fri, local team coverage. If customer is in EMEA/APAC and timing is critical, treat as one tier higher to account for time zone compression.

---

## Step-by-step workflow (CS/Support STO)
### Step 1 — Create a tracking ticket and identify the STO
Create a ticket in the internal system of record (Support/Jira or the designated GTM intake queue) with:
- Tier (P0/P1/P2)
- Due date/time zone
- Links/attachments to the questionnaire/RFP portal
- Requested artifacts list
- Deployment mode and region

Add watchers:
- AE + SE lead on the account
- GRC on-call analyst (or team alias)
- Security Engineering reviewer (if technical claims are involved)
- Legal reviewer (if contract language requested)

### Step 2 — Send the internal “first plan” message
Within the SLA window, post a clear plan (in the ticket and in the designated internal channel):
- What we will answer with standard language
- What requires review/approval
- What evidence requires NDA + controlled process
- Who owns each workstream and deadlines

### Step 3 — Separate “language” work from “evidence” work
Run two tracks in parallel:
A) Response language
- Use the Security FAQ and Standard Answers as the baseline.
- If the questionnaire asks for non-supported controls, use the Exceptions Policy to propose alternative language.
- If the customer requires a custom architecture/security narrative, SE drafts and Security validates.

B) Evidence requests
- Follow the SOC 2 Customer Evidence Request Playbook.
- Confirm NDA status before any restricted artifact is shared.
- Log exactly which artifacts were shared, when, and via what method.

### Step 4 — Run a time-boxed review cycle
For P0/P1, use a single redline pass with explicit approvers:
- Security Engineering: technical controls, logging, encryption, runtime behavior
- GRC: compliance posture wording, audit periods, “report under NDA” phrasing
- Legal: DPA/addendum terms, breach notification, liability language

If edits exceed one pass or the customer changes scope, re-baseline and reset expectations with Sales.

### Step 5 — Customer-facing delivery
CS/Support STO ensures:
- Final answers use approved language and correct deployment mode caveats
- Restricted artifacts are delivered only via the approved method
- The customer receives a concise “what we sent + how to follow up” summary

Recommended customer email structure:
- One-paragraph overview
- Bullets of attached/linked documents
- Evidence request steps (if applicable)
- Offer a 30-minute security review call with Security/GRC if needed

### Step 6 — Close the loop and create post-close handoff notes
Once the security review is complete (or “good enough” for procurement), capture:
- Final list of commitments made (e.g., log retention option selected, region selection)
- Any exceptions granted and their approvers
- Any open items that must be implemented/configured during onboarding

Add the notes to CRM and to the account’s implementation plan.

---

## Common scenarios and how to handle them
### Scenario A: “Send us your SOC 2 report today”
1) Confirm whether NDA is executed.
2) If NDA is not executed, coordinate with Legal/Sales immediately; do not share the report.
3) Use the approved wording: “SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA upon request.”
4) Open an evidence request per the playbook and track distribution.

### Scenario B: Customer asks “Do you train on our data?”
- Use the exact FAQ language and definitions (training vs transient processing; prompts/logs vs model weights).
- Do not introduce new qualifiers. If customer asks for contract language, route to Legal.

### Scenario C: EU data residency objection (must stay in EU)
- Confirm which regions are available for the chosen deployment mode.
- Use the approved residency language (no blanket promises). If constraints can only be met with Private, have SE present options.
- Escalate to GRC/Security if the customer requests written guarantees beyond standard documentation.

### Scenario D: Questionnaire asks for a control we do not support (e.g., specific IdP feature, custom audit event)
- Do not answer “Yes” with future intent.
- Use the Exceptions Policy to provide alternative language and document compensating controls.
- If customer insists on a “must-have,” flag to Product Security PM for capability alignment (without committing roadmap).

---

## Communication channels and meeting guidance
### Internal channels (recommended)
- Use the designated security review intake channel and link the tracking ticket.
- Keep decisions in the ticket. Slack is for coordination, not for the authoritative record.

### Customer call structure (30–45 minutes)
1) Confirm deployment mode + region + data flow expectations
2) Walk through top 5 controls customer cares about (usually: data use, encryption, access controls, logging, retention)
3) Evidence requests: explain NDA gating and timelines
4) Capture remaining blockers and assign owners

Avoid:
- Live “off the cuff” answers to compliance/certification questions. Offer to follow up with approved language.

---

## Handback to CS/Support after close (operationalization)
If any of the following were discussed, CS must validate configuration during onboarding:
- Audit log export destination (SIEM/S3) and retention window
- SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning requirements
- RBAC roles and least-privilege model for admins
- Data retention/deletion configuration for the chosen deployment mode
- Private deployment network boundaries (VPC peering, egress controls) and key management (KMS/HSM)

Create an onboarding checklist item for each requirement and confirm acceptance criteria with the customer security contact.

---

## Templates
### Internal escalation summary (paste into ticket)
Account:
Deployment mode:
Region(s):
Tier (P0/P1/P2):
Customer deadline (date/time zone):
Top asks (verbatim):
Artifacts requested:
NDA status:
Draft response plan (what we can answer with standard language vs needs review):
Owners:

### Customer follow-up email (minimal)
Subject: Redwood security review materials + next steps

Hi <Name>,

Sharing the requested security materials for your review:
- <Doc link 1>
- <Doc link 2>
- <Audit logging / retention overview>

For the SOC 2 Type II report (restricted), we can provide it under NDA via our controlled evidence request process. If you confirm NDA status, we will initiate distribution.

Happy to schedule a 30-minute security review call to walk through data handling, encryption, access controls, and audit logging.

Best,
<Name>

---

## Metrics and continuous improvement
CS/Support STO should log the following for quarterly review:
- Time-to-acknowledge and time-to-first-draft by tier
- # of evidence requests and average turnaround time
- Top repeated questionnaire questions and where our standard language was insufficient
- Any instances of “unapproved language” caught in review (and required remediation)

Feedback loop:
- If a question repeats \>= 3 times in a month, open a request to update the Security FAQ or RFP library rather than rewriting per deal.

---

## Ownership and review cadence
Owner: Customer Success (CS sponsor), in partnership with Security/GRC.
Review cadence: Quarterly, or immediately after any material change to security posture, evidence availability, or product behavior affecting common questionnaire answers.

Last review highlights (2026-02-21):
- Tightened P0/P1 SLA expectations and clarified NDA gating for evidence.
- Standardized separation of “language” vs “evidence” workstreams.
- Added explicit post-close operationalization checklist items (SSO/SCIM, audit logs, retention).",

item.text: The evidence converges on a strict rule: residency gating precedes availability. For an EU-only or region-pinned tenant, an unhealthy allowed set produces in-boundary degradation—not an unapproved non-EU failover. I’m encoding that deny default, plus KMS fail-closed checks and audit/export requirements, while flagging the remaining contract/control-plane ambiguities.

A formatting delimiter in the workspace-write payload was rejected before either file was written. I’m correcting the payload and preserving the same reviewed content; no branch state was partially published or indexed.

# EU residency interview notes (private working state)

Status: provisional; do not index or publish.
Owner: Jada Williams
Date: 2026-08-14

## Working synthesis
- Hosted Enterprise supports EU-only, region-pinned, and contract-defined boundaries.
- Reviewed security policy makes residency an absolute data-plane gate. No availability exception exists without Security and customer approval plus an incident record.
- Informal references to DR consent describe an explicitly contracted custom boundary, not authority to bypass EU-only policy.
- CMEK remains regional. Validate target-region key, state, grants, endpoint, and test operation. Fail closed; never substitute an unrelated key.
- Audit recommendation, execution, rollback, override, and blocked decisions without payloads.
- Support must validate contract, policy, KMS, and evidence and avoid unapproved guarantees.

## Open points
- Exact control-plane fields and their contract treatment are unresolved.
- Security cites 180-day internal and >=400-day add-on retention but flags enterprise-default alignment for follow-up.
- Live region/model inventory and KMS mappings remain authoritative configuration.

# EU Residency Failover — Hosted API Support Runbook

Status: Reviewed
Owner: Platform Engineering (Jada Williams)
Audience: Support, Customer Success, Incident Command, SRE, Security/GRC
Reviewed: 2026-08-14

## Controlling rule

Residency precedes availability. The router may select only a healthy region inside the tenant's effective allow-list. If no allowed target is healthy and capable, protect or degrade service in-boundary (including retryable 503/429); never route outside the boundary. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)

## Supported routing modes

| Mode | Allowed | Denied |
|---|---|---|
| EU-only multi-region | Fail over among explicitly allowed, healthy EU regions after control validation. | Non-EU data-plane processing. |
| Region-pinned EU | Stay in-region; use protection, load shedding, feature reduction, and retryable errors. | Every cross-region failover. |
| Contract-defined custom boundary | Use only contract-named, policy-encoded regions; honor manual approvals. | Any non-listed region or pool. |
| Global/no residency | Route under normal healthy-region policy. | Treating global status as an EU commitment. |

Residency covers prompts, inputs, outputs, embeddings, and tool/function payloads. Control-plane tenant/config/quota/routing metadata and operational telemetry may be replicated under separate security policies; do not promise that all control-plane data is EU-only unless the executed contract says so. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)

Hosted Enterprise commitments must be encoded as enforceable policy. Policy resolution must be deterministic and expose effective policy, allowed regions, primary, outcome, selected region, reason, and rule. [Hosted Residency Enforcement PRD; dsid_eae602f3def843a5ab022d14e9d84ddf](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/hosted-data-residency-enforcement-prd.json)

## Consent and deny defaults

1. Read the executed Hosted Enterprise agreement/Data Residency Addendum; record boundary, approval mode, notification, and audit terms.
2. Compare it with effective org/project/key policy and immutable revision.
3. Missing, stale, contradictory, or unreadable consent means deny. Never infer consent from an outage, ticket, label, or conversation.
4. Broader processing is valid only where contract scope is explicit and the corresponding regions are already allow-listed. Customer guidance says non-EU paths require documented contractual consent; EU-tagged backups are region-bound by default and are not replicated outside EU unless requested. [Cross-border clarification; dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json)
5. Never temporarily bypass EU-only policy. An incident-time boundary change requires Security delegate approval, explicit customer approval, and timestamped scope. Until all exist and policy is safely revised, degrade in-boundary. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)

## KMS/CMEK

Before routing to an allowed target:

- Resolve the tenant's configured regional key mapping; never substitute an unrelated key.
- Verify key exists, is enabled, is not pending deletion, and matches expected region/account.
- Verify runtime principal and key policy grant required encrypt/decrypt operations.
- Verify regional endpoint reachability and run a non-customer-data test operation.
- Verify required snapshots/artifacts use a permitted regional key and replication matches contract.
- Redact/normalize sensitive key identifiers in exports.

Hosted CMEK guidance says key material remains in the customer's KMS region. [Cross-border clarification; dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json) Wrong region, missing/disabled key, AccessDenied, or failed test is fail-closed/no-go: no excessive retries, unrelated-key fallback, or target traffic. [KMS failure modes matrix; dsid_13ce99fab0df4c76ad68d572dbbca7c0](/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/kms-failure-modes-test-matrix-sheet.json) Coordinate Hosted/Dedicated IAM or policy faults with Eng Infra/Platform. [KMS decrypt failures; dsid_620102a3964a4ef1969850909f59eeae](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/kms-decrypt-failures-runbook.json)

## Audit commitments

Emit events for recommendation/dry-run, execution, rollback, override, and residency-blocked actions. Capture UTC timestamp; tenant/org stable ID and tier; residency category; primary/target; decision; reason; health/probe/alert evidence; actor; approval state; routing revision; and incident/request/dashboard correlations. Never include prompts, outputs, embeddings, payloads, secrets, or API keys.

Reviewed security guidance states 180-day internal retention and >=400 days for add-on/compliance packages unless otherwise specified. Raw access is restricted to necessary SRE/routing staff and Security/Compliance; Support/CS receives approved redacted exports. Because enterprise-default alignment is an open follow-up, quote only the customer's executed retention term externally. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)

## Validation

### Before

1. Associate an incident; identify customer, tenant, mode, tier, and contract.
2. Capture residency clause, allowed set, consent/approval mode, and audit/notification terms.
3. Resolve policy at every scope; record final allow-list and revision.
4. Confirm target is allow-listed, healthy, capable, and supports required model/features using live routing config.
5. Complete regional KMS checks.
6. Run dry-run; verify expected decision/reason, audit delivery, and annotation.
7. For tests, exclude pinned/regulated tenants without written approval; validate blocked actions are observable.
8. Obtain contract-required customer/operator acknowledgement and SRE/Security approval.

### During and after

1. Execute only the reviewed revision; monitor errors, latency, capacity, KMS, and residency drift.
2. Confirm audit records have correct tenant, regions, actor, approval, evidence, and change/incident IDs.
3. Use synthetic/data-minimized probes and tenant observations to confirm only allowed regions.
4. On failure, stop/rollback inside the allowed boundary and escalate.
5. Communicate impact, scope, mitigation, and confidence; never promise zero impact. [Regional Failover Communication Playbook; dsid_f1e9331031a8466dadc67270525b36eb](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/regional-failover-communication-playbook.json)
6. Preserve audit summary, revisions, approvals, probes, KMS evidence, timestamps, and notices.
7. Before closure, confirm final routing, no out-of-boundary processing, and contracted export/notice fulfillment.

## Escalate immediately

- Contract, addendum, tag, and effective policy disagree or are unavailable.
- Suggested/observed target is outside boundary, or an EU tenant appears on a non-EU primary.
- No healthy/capable allowed target exists.
- Consent or required approval is missing/ambiguous.
- Any KMS region, state, permission, endpoint, decrypt, or encryption check fails.
- Audit evidence is missing, delayed, malformed, contains payload data, or cannot prove the decision.
- Drift/customer reports possible out-of-boundary processing.
- An incident-time boundary change or override is proposed.
- Customer requests guarantees beyond approved language, NDA-gated evidence, or contract interpretation.

Route technical incidents to IC/SRE and Routing/Platform; suspected residency violations to Security/GRC and Legal/Privacy; contract ambiguity to Legal/account owner. Support handoff records mode, regions, exact ask, requested artifacts, deadline/time zone, NDA status, red lines, and owners, and avoids off-the-cuff promises. [Support security-review handoff; dsid_2ea8e611a8b448ffab3bc5b927a3d466](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/security-review-escalation-and-handoff.json)

## Reviewed support response rule

> Redwood applies the residency boundary configured for your Hosted API tenant before selecting a failover target. For an EU-only tenant, traffic may move only to a healthy, explicitly allowed EU region. A single-region pin does not fail over cross-region. If no permitted target is available, we keep processing within the boundary and may degrade or return retryable errors rather than route outside it. Any broader contract-defined boundary must be explicitly consented to and encoded in policy; missing or conflicting consent is denied. Before a permitted failover, we validate the target's regional KMS/CMEK mapping and access and fail closed on key or permission errors. We record the decision, approvals, execution or block, and rollback without customer payloads, and provide audit evidence according to your contract and approved export process.

Do not add exact regions, RTO/RPO, control-plane residency, retention, zero-impact, or notification claims until verified against live configuration and executed terms.

## Remaining uncertainty

- Customer-specific contract language, consent form, RTO/RPO, cadence, and export entitlement require per-account checks.
- Exact control-plane field inventory and EU contract treatment are not established by cited sources.
- Security retention baselines exist, but enterprise-default alignment remains unresolved.
- Supported regions, models/features, capacity, and KMS mappings are live configuration.
- Informal sources describe DR consent imprecisely; this runbook follows the stricter reviewed rule that routing never leaves the effective boundary.

Any broader contract-defined boundary must be explicitly consented to and encoded in policy; missing or conflicting consent is denied. Before a permitted failover, we validate the target's regional KMS/CMEK mapping and access and fail closed on key or permission errors. We record the decision, approvals, execution or block, and rollback without customer payloads, and provide audit evidence according to your contract and approved export process.

Do not add exact regions, RTO/RPO, control-plane residency, retention, zero-impact, or notification claims until verified against live configuration and executed terms.

## Remaining uncertainty

- Customer-specific contract language, consent form, RTO/RPO, cadence, and export entitlement require per-account checks.
- Exact control-plane field inventory and EU contract treatment are not established by cited sources.
- Security retention baselines exist, but enterprise-default alignment remains unresolved.
- Supported regions, models/features, capacity, and KMS mappings are live configuration.
- Informal sources describe DR consent imprecisely; this runbook follows the stricter reviewed rule that routing never leaves the effective boundary.

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover — Hosted API Support Runbook\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-eu-residency-failover-20260814\n\n# EU Residency Failover — Hosted API Support Runbook\n\nStatus: Reviewed\nOwner: Platform Engineering (Jada Williams)\nAudience: Support, Customer Success, Incident Command, SRE, Security/GRC\nReviewed: 2026-08-14\n\n## Controlling rule\n\nResidency precedes availability. The router may select only a healthy region inside the tenant's effective allow-list. If no allowed target is healthy and capable, protect or degrade service in-boundary (including retryable 503/429); never route outside the boundary. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)\n\n## Supported routing modes\n\n| Mode | Allowed | Denied |\n|---|---|---|\n| EU-only multi-region | Fail over among explicitly allowed, healthy EU regions after control validation. | Non-EU data-plane processing. |\n| Region-pinned EU | Stay in-region; use protection, load shedding, feature reduction, and retryable errors. | Every cross-region failover. |\n| Contract-defined custom boundary | Use only contract-named, policy-encoded regions; honor manual approvals. | Any non-listed region or pool. |\n| Global/no residency | Route under normal healthy-region policy. | Treating global status as an EU commitment. |\n\nResidency covers prompts, inputs, outputs, embeddings, and tool/function payloads. Control-plane tenant/config/quota/routing metadata and operational telemetry may be replicated under separate security policies; do not promise that all control-plane data is EU-only unless the executed contract says so. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)",

Policy resolution must be deterministic and expose effective policy, allowed regions, primary, outcome, selected region, reason, and rule. [Hosted Residency Enforcement PRD; dsid_eae602f3def843a5ab022d14e9d84ddf](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/hosted-data-residency-enforcement-prd.json)\n\n## Consent and deny defaults\n\n1. Read the executed Hosted Enterprise agreement/Data Residency Addendum; record boundary, approval mode, notification, and audit terms.\n2. Compare it with effective org/project/key policy and immutable revision.\n3. Missing, stale, contradictory, or unreadable consent means deny. Never infer consent from an outage, ticket, label, or conversation.\n4. Broader processing is valid only where contract scope is explicit and the corresponding regions are already allow-listed. Customer guidance says non-EU paths require documented contractual consent; EU-tagged backups are region-bound by default and are not replicated outside EU unless requested. [Cross-border clarification; dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json)\n5.               "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover — Hosted API Support Runbook\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-eu-residency-failover-20260814\n\nFailover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)\n\n## KMS/CMEK\n\nBefore routing to an allowed target:\n\n- Resolve the tenant's configured regional key mapping; never substitute an unrelated key.\n- Verify key exists, is enabled, is not pending deletion, and matches expected region/account.\n- Verify runtime principal and key policy grant required encrypt/decrypt operations.\n- Verify regional endpoint reachability and run a non-customer-data test operation.\n- Verify required snapshots/artifacts use a permitted regional key and replication matches contract.\n- Redact/normalize sensitive key identifiers in exports.\n\nHosted CMEK guidance says key material remains in the customer's KMS region. Capture UTC timestamp; tenant/org stable ID and tier; residency category; primary/target; decision; reason; health/probe/alert evidence; actor; approval state; routing revision; and incident/request/dashboard correlations. Never include prompts, outputs, embeddings, payloads, secrets, or API keys.\n\nReviewed security guidance states 180-day internal retention and >=400 days for add-on/compliance packages unless otherwise specified. Raw access is restricted to necessary SRE/routing staff and Security/Compliance; Support/CS receives approved redacted exports. Because enterprise-default alignment is an open follow-up, quote only the customer's executed retention term externally. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)\n\n## Validation\n\n### Before\n\n1. Associate an incident; identify customer, tenant, mode, tier, and contract.\n2. Capture residency clause, allowed set, consent/approval mode, and audit/notification terms.\n3. Resolve policy at every scope; record final allow-list and revision.\n4. Confirm target is allow-listed, healthy, capable, and supports required model/features using live routing config.\n5. Complete regional KMS checks.\n6. Run dry-run; verify expected decision/reason, audit delivery, and annotation.\n7. For tests, exclude pinned/regulated tenants without written approval; validate blocked actions are observable.\n8.               "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover — Hosted API Support Runbook\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-eu-residency-failover-20260814\n\nComplete regional KMS checks.\n6. Run dry-run; verify expected decision/reason, audit delivery, and annotation.\n7. For tests, exclude pinned/regulated tenants without written approval; validate blocked actions are observable.\n8. Obtain contract-required customer/operator acknowledgement and SRE/Security approval.\n\n### During and after\n\n1. Execute only the reviewed revision; monitor errors, latency, capacity, KMS, and residency drift.\n2. Confirm audit records have correct tenant, regions, actor, approval, evidence, and change/incident IDs.\n3. Use synthetic/data-minimized probes and tenant observations to confirm only allowed regions.\n4. On failure, stop/rollback inside the allowed boundary and escalate.\n5. Communicate impact, scope, mitigation, and confidence; never promise zero impact. [Regional Failover Communication Playbook; dsid_f1e9331031a8466dadc67270525b36eb](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/regional-failover-communication-playbook.json)\n6. Preserve audit summary, revisions, approvals, probes, KMS evidence, timestamps, and notices.\n7. Before closure, confirm final routing, no out-of-boundary processing, and contracted export/notice fulfillment.\n\n## Escalate immediately\n\n- Contract, addendum, tag, and effective policy disagree or are unavailable.\n- Suggested/observed target is outside boundary, or an EU tenant appears on a non-EU primary.\n- No healthy/capable allowed target exists.\n- Consent or required approval is missing/ambiguous.\n- Any KMS region, state, permission, endpoint, decrypt, or encryption check fails.\n- Audit evidence is missing, delayed, malformed, contains payload data, or cannot prove the decision.\n- Drift/customer reports possible out-of-boundary processing.\n- An incident-time boundary change or override is proposed.\n- Customer requests guarantees beyond approved language, NDA-gated evidence, or contract interpretation.",

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: EU Residency Failover — Hosted API Support Runbook\nSource: Redwood Inference / Platform Engineering\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/eu-residency-failover.md\nWorkspace: task/jada-eu-residency-failover-20260814\n\ncheck fails.\n- Audit evidence is missing, delayed, malformed, contains payload data, or cannot prove the decision.\n- Drift/customer reports possible out-of-boundary processing.\n- An incident-time boundary change or override is proposed.\n- Customer requests guarantees beyond approved language, NDA-gated evidence, or contract interpretation.\n\nRoute technical incidents to IC/SRE and Routing/Platform; suspected residency violations to Security/GRC and Legal/Privacy; contract ambiguity to Legal/account owner. Support handoff records mode, regions, exact ask, requested artifacts, deadline/time zone, NDA status, red lines, and owners, and avoids off-the-cuff promises. [Support security-review handoff; dsid_2ea8e611a8b448ffab3bc5b927a3d466](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/security-review-escalation-and-handoff.json)\n\n## Reviewed support response rule\n\n> Redwood applies the residency boundary configured for your Hosted API tenant before selecting a failover target. For an EU-only tenant, traffic may move only to a healthy, explicitly allowed EU region. A single-region pin does not fail over cross-region. If no permitted target is available, we keep processing within the boundary and may degrade or return retryable errors rather than route outside it. Any broader contract-defined boundary must be explicitly consented to and encoded in policy; missing or conflicting consent is denied. Before a permitted failover, we validate the target's regional KMS/CMEK mapping and access and fail closed on key or permission errors. We record the decision, approvals, execution or block, and rollback without customer payloads, and provide audit evidence according to your contract and approved export process.\n\nDo not add exact regions, RTO/RPO, control-plane residency, retention, zero-impact, or notification claims until verified against live configuration and executed terms.\n\n## Remaining uncertainty",

            "content": "# EU residency interview notes (private working state)\n\nStatus: provisional; do not index or publish.\nOwner: Jada Williams\nDate: 2026-08-14\n\n## Working synthesis\n- Hosted Enterprise supports EU-only, region-pinned, and contract-defined boundaries.\n- Reviewed security policy makes residency an absolute data-plane gate. Validate target-region key, state, grants, endpoint, and test operation.             "content": "# EU Residency Failover — Hosted API Support Runbook\n\nStatus: Reviewed\nOwner: Platform Engineering (Jada Williams)\nAudience: Support, Customer Success, Incident Command, SRE, Security/GRC\nReviewed: 2026-08-14\n\n## Controlling rule\n\nResidency precedes availability. The router may select only a healthy region inside the tenant's effective allow-list. If no allowed target is healthy and capable, protect or degrade service in-boundary (including retryable 503/429); never route outside the boundary. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)\n\n## Supported routing modes\n\n| Mode | Allowed | Denied |\n|---|---|---|\n| EU-only multi-region | Fail over among explicitly allowed, healthy EU regions after control validation. | Non-EU data-plane processing. |\n| Region-pinned EU | Stay in-region; use protection, load shedding, feature reduction, and retryable errors. | Every cross-region failover. |\n| Contract-defined custom boundary | Use only contract-named, policy-encoded regions; honor manual approvals. | Any non-listed region or pool. |\n| Global/no residency | Route under normal healthy-region policy. | Treating global status as an EU commitment. |\n\nResidency covers prompts, inputs, outputs, embeddings, and tool/function payloads. Control-plane tenant/config/quota/routing metadata and operational telemetry may be replicated under separate security policies; do not promise that all control-plane data is EU-only unless the executed contract says so. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)\n\nHosted Enterprise commitments must be encoded as enforceable policy. Policy resolution must be deterministic and expose effective policy, allowed regions, primary, outcome, selected region, reason, and rule. [Hosted Residency Enforcement PRD; dsid_eae602f3def843a5ab022d14e9d84ddf](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/hosted-data-residency-enforcement-prd.json)\n\n## Consent and deny defaults\n\n1. Read the executed Hosted Enterprise agreement/Data Residency Addendum; record boundary, approval mode, notification, and audit terms.\n2. Compare it with effective org/project/key policy and immutable revision.\n3. Missing, stale, contradictory, or unreadable consent means deny. Never infer consent from an outage, ticket, label, or conversation.\n4. Broader processing is valid only where contract scope is explicit and the corresponding regions are already allow-listed. Customer guidance says non-EU paths require documented contractual consent; EU-tagged backups are region-bound by default and are not replicated outside EU unless requested. [Cross-border clarification; dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json)\n5. Never temporarily bypass EU-only policy. An incident-time boundary change requires Security delegate approval, explicit customer approval, and timestamped scope. Until all exist and policy is safely revised, degrade in-boundary. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)\n\n## KMS/CMEK\n\nBefore routing to an allowed target:\n\n- Resolve the tenant's configured regional key mapping; never substitute an unrelated key.\n- Verify key exists, is enabled, is not pending deletion, and matches expected region/account.\n- Verify runtime principal and key policy grant required encrypt/decrypt operations.\n- Verify regional endpoint reachability and run a non-customer-data test operation.\n- Verify required snapshots/artifacts use a permitted regional key and replication matches contract.\n- Redact/normalize sensitive key identifiers in exports.\n\nHosted CMEK guidance says key materi",

[KMS failure modes matrix; dsid_13ce99fab0df4c76ad68d572dbbca7c0](/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/kms-failure-modes-test-matrix-sheet.json) Coordinate Hosted/Dedicated IAM or policy faults with Eng Infra/Platform. [KMS decrypt failures; dsid_620102a3964a4ef1969850909f59eeae](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/kms-decrypt-failures-runbook.json)\n\n## Audit commitments\n\nEmit events for recommendation/dry-run, execution, rollback, override, and residency-blocked actions. Capture UTC timestamp; tenant/org stable ID and tier; residency category; primary/target; decision; reason; health/probe/alert evidence; actor; approval state; routing revision; and incident/request/dashboard correlations. Never include prompts, outputs, embeddings, payloads, secrets, or API keys.\n\nReviewed security guidance states 180-day internal retention and >=400 days for add-on/compliance packages unless otherwise specified. Raw access is restricted to necessary SRE/routing staff and Security/Compliance; Support/CS receives approved redacted exports. Because enterprise-default alignment is an open follow-up, quote only the customer's executed retention term externally. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)\n\n## Validation\n\n### Before\n\n1. Associate an incident; identify customer, tenant, mode, tier, and contract.\n2. Capture residency clause, allowed set, consent/approval mode, and audit/notification terms.\n3. Resolve policy at every scope; record final allow-list and revision.\n4. Confirm target is allow-listed, healthy, capable, and supports required model/features using live routing config.\n5. Complete regional KMS checks.\n6. Run dry-run; verify expected decision/reason, audit delivery, and annotation.\n7. For tests, exclude pinned/regulated tenants without written approval; validate blocked actions are observable.\n8. Obtain contract-required customer/operator acknowledgement and SRE/Security approval.\n\n### During and after\n\n1. Execute only the reviewed revision; monitor errors, latency, capacity, KMS, and residency drift.\n2. Confirm audit records have correct tenant, regions, actor, approval, evidence, and change/incident IDs.\n3. Use synthetic/data-minimized probes and tenant observations to confirm only allowed regions.\n4. On failure, stop/rollback inside the allowed boundary and escalate.\n5. Communicate impact, scope, mitigation, and confidence; never promise zero impact. [Regional Failover Communication Playbook; dsid_f1e9331031a8466dadc67270525b36eb](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/regional-failover-communication-playbook.json)\n6. Preserve audit summary, revisions, approvals, probes, KMS evidence, timestamps, and notices.\n7. Before closure, confirm final routing, no out-of-boundary processing, and contracted export/notice fulfillment.\n\n## Escalate immediately\n\n- Contract, addendum, tag, and effective policy disagree or are unavailable.\n- Suggested/observed target is outside boundary, or an EU tenant appears on a non-EU primary.\n- No healthy/capable allowed target exists.\n- Consent or required approval is missing/ambiguous.\n- Any KMS region, state, permission, endpoint, decrypt, or encryption check fails.\n- Audit evidence is missing, delayed, malformed, contains payload data, or cannot prove the decision.\n- Drift/customer reports possible out-of-boundary processing.\n- An incident-time boundary change or override is proposed.\n- Customer requests guarantees beyond approved language, NDA-gated evidence, or ",

            "content": "contract interpretation.\n\nRoute technical incidents to IC/SRE and Routing/Platform; suspected residency violations to Security/GRC and Legal/Privacy; contract ambiguity to Legal/account owner. Support handoff records mode, regions, exact ask, requested artifacts, deadline/time zone, NDA status, red lines, and owners, and avoids off-the-cuff promises. [Support security-review handoff; dsid_2ea8e611a8b448ffab3bc5b927a3d466](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/security-review-escalation-and-handoff.json)\n\n## Reviewed support response rule\n\n> Redwood applies the residency boundary configured for your Hosted API tenant before selecting a failover target. For an EU-only tenant, traffic may move only to a healthy, explicitly allowed EU region. A single-region pin does not fail over cross-region. If no permitted target is available, we keep processing within the boundary and may degrade or return retryable errors rather than route outside it. # EU Residency Failover — Hosted API Support Runbook

Status: Reviewed
Owner: Platform Engineering (Jada Williams)
Audience: Support, Customer Success, Incident Command, SRE, Security/GRC
Reviewed: 2026-08-14

## Controlling rule

Residency precedes availability. The router may select only a healthy region inside the tenant's effective allow-list. If no allowed target is healthy and capable, protect or degrade service in-boundary (including retryable 503/429); never route outside the boundary. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)

## Supported routing modes

| Mode | Allowed | Denied |
|---|---|---|
| EU-only multi-region | Fail over among explicitly allowed, healthy EU regions after control validation. | Non-EU data-plane processing. |
| Region-pinned EU | Stay in-region; use protection, load shedding, feature reduction, and retryable errors. | Every cross-region failover. |
| Contract-defined custom boundary | Use only contract-named, policy-encoded regions; honor manual approvals. | Any non-listed region or pool. |
| Global/no residency | Route under normal healthy-region policy. | Treating global status as an EU commitment. |

Residency covers prompts, inputs, outputs, embeddings, and tool/function payloads. Control-plane tenant/config/quota/routing metadata and operational telemetry may be replicated under separate security policies; do not promise that all control-plane data is EU-only unless the executed contract says so. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)

Hosted Enterprise commitments must be encoded as enforceable policy. Policy resolution must be deterministic and expose effective policy, allowed regions, primary, outcome, selected region, reason, and rule. [Hosted Residency Enforcement PRD; dsid_eae602f3def843a5ab022d14e9d84ddf](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/hosted-data-residency-enforcement-prd.json)

## Consent and deny defaults

1. Read the executed Hosted Enterprise agreement/Data Residency Addendum; record boundary, approval mode, notification, and audit terms.
2. Compare it with effective org/project/key policy and immutable revision.
3. Missing, stale, contradictory, or unreadable consent means deny. Never infer consent from an outage, ticket, label, or conversation.
4. Broader processing is valid only where contract scope is explicit and the corresponding regions are already allow-listed. Customer guidance says non-EU paths require documented contractual consent; EU-tagged backups are region-bound by default and are not replicated outside EU unless requested. [Cross-border clarification; dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json)
5. Never temporarily bypass EU-only policy. An incident-time boundary change requires Security delegate approval, explicit customer approval, and timestamped scope. Until all exist and policy is safely revised, degrade in-boundary. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)

## KMS/CMEK

Before routing to an allowed target:

## KMS/CMEK

Before routing to an allowed target:

- Resolve the tenant's configured regional key mapping; never substitute an unrelated key.
- Verify key exists, is enabled, is not pending deletion, and matches expected region/account.
- Verify runtime principal and key policy grant required encrypt/decrypt operations.
- Verify regional endpoint reachability and run a non-customer-data test operation.
- Verify required snapshots/artifacts use a permitted regional key and replication matches contract.
- Redact/normalize sensitive key identifiers in exports.

Hosted CMEK guidance says key material remains in the customer's KMS region. [Cross-border clarification; dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json) Wrong region, missing/disabled key, AccessDenied, or failed test is fail-closed/no-go: no excessive retries, unrelated-key fallback, or target traffic. [KMS failure modes matrix; dsid_13ce99fab0df4c76ad68d572dbbca7c0](/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/kms-failure-modes-test-matrix-sheet.json) Coordinate Hosted/Dedicated IAM or policy faults with Eng Infra/Platform. [KMS decrypt failures; dsid_620102a3964a4ef1969850909f59eeae](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/kms-decrypt-failures-runbook.json)

## Audit commitments

## Audit commitments

Emit events for recommendation/dry-run, execution, rollback, override, and residency-blocked actions. Capture UTC timestamp; tenant/org stable ID and tier; residency category; primary/target; decision; reason; health/probe/alert evidence; actor; approval state; routing revision; and incident/request/dashboard correlations. Never include prompts, outputs, embeddings, payloads, secrets, or API keys.

Reviewed security guidance states 180-day internal retention and >=400 days for add-on/compliance packages unless otherwise specified. Raw access is restricted to necessary SRE/routing staff and Security/Compliance; Support/CS receives approved redacted exports. Because enterprise-default alignment is an open follow-up, quote only the customer's executed retention term externally. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)

## Validation

### Before

1. Associate an incident; identify customer, tenant, mode, tier, and contract.
2. Capture residency clause, allowed set, consent/approval mode, and audit/notification terms.
3. Resolve policy at every scope; record final allow-list and revision.
4. Confirm target is allow-listed, healthy, capable, and supports required model/features using live routing config.
5. Complete regional KMS checks.
6. Run dry-run; verify expected decision/reason, audit delivery, and annotation.
7. For tests, exclude pinned/regulated tenants without written approval; validate blocked actions are observable.
8. Obtain contract-required customer/operator acknowledgement and SRE/Security approval.

### During and after

7. For tests, exclude pinned/regulated tenants without written approval; validate blocked actions are observable.
8. Obtain contract-required customer/operator acknowledgement and SRE/Security approval.

### During and after

1. Execute only the reviewed revision; monitor errors, latency, capacity, KMS, and residency drift.
2. Confirm audit records have correct tenant, regions, actor, approval, evidence, and change/incident IDs.
3. Use synthetic/data-minimized probes and tenant observations to confirm only allowed regions.
4. On failure, stop/rollback inside the allowed boundary and escalate.
5. Communicate impact, scope, mitigation, and confidence; never promise zero impact. [Regional Failover Communication Playbook; dsid_f1e9331031a8466dadc67270525b36eb](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process/regional-failover-communication-playbook.json)
6. Preserve audit summary, revisions, approvals, probes, KMS evidence, timestamps, and notices.
7. Before closure, confirm final routing, no out-of-boundary processing, and contracted export/notice fulfillment.

## Escalate immediately

- Contract, addendum, tag, and effective policy disagree or are unavailable.
- Suggested/observed target is outside boundary, or an EU tenant appears on a non-EU primary.
- No healthy/capable allowed target exists.
- Consent or required approval is missing/ambiguous.
- Any KMS region, state, permission, endpoint, decrypt, or encryption check fails.
- Audit evidence is missing, delayed, malformed, contains payload data, or cannot prove the decision.
- Drift/customer reports possible out-of-boundary processing.
- An incident-time boundary change or override is proposed.
- Customer requests guarantees beyond approved language, NDA-gated evidence, or contract interpretation.

Status: Reviewed
Owner: Platform Engineering (Jada Williams)
Audience: Support, Customer Success, Incident Command, SRE, Security/GRC

## Controlling rule

Residency precedes availability. The router may select only a healthy region inside the tenant's effective allow-list. If no allowed target is healthy and capable, protect or degrade service in-boundary (including retryable 503/429); never route outside the boundary. ## Supported routing modes

| Mode | Allowed | Denied |
|---|---|---|
| EU-only multi-region | Fail over among explicitly allowed, healthy EU regions after control validation. | Non-EU data-plane processing. |
| Region-pinned EU | Stay in-region; use protection, load shedding, feature reduction, and retryable errors. | Every cross-region failover. |
| Contract-defined custom boundary | Use only contract-named, policy-encoded regions; honor manual approvals. | Any non-listed region or pool. |
| Global/no residency | Route under normal healthy-region policy. | Treating global status as an EU commitment. |

Residency covers prompts, inputs, outputs, embeddings, and tool/function payloads. Control-plane tenant/config/quota/routing metadata and operational telemetry may be replicated under separate security policies; do not promise that all control-plane data is EU-only unless the executed contract says so. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)

Policy resolution must be deterministic and expose effective policy, allowed regions, primary, outcome, selected region, reason, and rule. ## Consent and deny defaults

1. Read the executed Hosted Enterprise agreement/Data Residency Addendum; record boundary, approval mode, notification, and audit terms.
2. Compare it with effective org/project/key policy and immutable revision.
3. Missing, stale, contradictory, or unreadable consent means deny. Never infer consent from an outage, ticket, label, or conversation.
4. Broader processing is valid only where contract scope is explicit and the corresponding regions are already allow-listed. Customer guidance says non-EU paths require documented contractual consent; EU-tagged backups are region-bound by default and are not replicated outside EU unless requested. [Cross-border clarification; dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json)
5. Never temporarily bypass EU-only policy. An incident-time boundary change requires Security delegate approval, explicit customer approval, and timestamped scope. Until all exist and policy is safely revised, degrade in-boundary. [Failover and Security Boundaries; dsid_e86ea669ce674d9e87dd8712dd738349](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/failover-and-security-boundaries.json)

Before routing to an allowed target:

- Resolve the tenant's configured regional key mapping; never substitute an unrelated key.

- Verify regional endpoint reachability and run a non-customer-data test operation.
- Verify required snapshots/artifacts use a permitted regional key and replication matches contract.
- Redact/normalize sensitive key identifiers in exports.

Hosted CMEK guidance says key materi

al remains in the customer's KMS region. [Cross-border clarification; dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json) Wrong region, missing/disabled key, AccessDenied, or failed test is fail-closed/no-go: no excessive retries, unrelated-key fallback, or target traffic. Emit events for recommendation/dry-run, execution, rollback, override, and residency-blocked actions. Policy resolution must be deterministic and expose effective policy, allowed regions, primary, outcome, selected region, reason, and rule. Read the executed Hosted Enterprise agreement/Data Residency Addendum; record boundary, approval mode, notification, and audit terms.\n2. Compare it with effective org/project/key policy and immutable revision.\n3. Missing, stale, contradictory, or unreadable consent means deny. Never infer consent from an outage, ticket, label, or conversation.\n4. Broader processing is valid only where contract scope is explicit and the corresponding regions are already allow-listed. Customer guidance says non-EU paths require documented contractual consent; EU-tagged backups are region-bound by default and are not replicated outside EU unless requested. [Cross-border clarification; dsid_2f34daefcf1544f58612fd2f91746ee4](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260212-residency-retention-clarify-cross-border.json)\n5.
